# Changelog

All notable changes to Pragmatica will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/).

## [1.0.0-rc4] - Unreleased

### Changed (2026-10-16 — #2214: rc4 known limitations — no-majority network cut, bootstrap re-run)
- **Known limitation: a network cut that leaves no core majority halts every core.** If no group of cores holds a majority for long enough, each core drains and exits with code 2 and is not restarted (`Restart=no`); a heal after a core has begun draining does not cancel its halt. Consensus state is memory-only, so blueprints, slice targets, API keys, cluster and stream configuration and entity state are lost. Measured with every core isolated from every other on five cores: a 10 s cut halted 0 of 25 core-runs, 15 s halted 2 of 25, and 20 s, 25 s and 30 s halted 25 of 25 each; the drain began 18-19 s after the cut (3-4 s detection plus the 15 s `split_timeout`); 77 of 77 cores that fired exited with code 2 and none returned. `[measured: five-node Ember probe on the rc4 tip, loopback on one host; the probe is not in the repository]` Not measured: a 2/2/1 split, cut lengths of 16-19 s, other `split_timeout` values, a production-mode halt. `[unverified: those four]`
- **Mitigation and recovery.** Configure `[backup]` with a `remote` on every multi-core production cluster (`runbooks/deployment.md`); the backup holds declared state up to the last successful push, not entity state or acknowledged stream records. Recovery is the fresh-NodeId restore in `runbooks/backup-recovery.md`; the procedure is the new "No-majority partition / every core halted" section of `runbooks/incident-response.md`. `[mechanism: DrainProcedure.java:186-199 single-shot drain; BackupConfig.java:56,70 backup off by default]`
- **Known limitation: what the fresh-bootstrap name check (#2213) does not cover.** A fresh `aether cluster bootstrap` refuses when the registry, a local bootstrap state or (cloud sources only) a labelled provider instance shows the name. SSH and Docker hosts are not listed, a cluster known only to another workstation is seen only through cloud labels, no lock is taken between two concurrent bootstraps, and `destroy` of a name still removes every machine labelled `aether-cluster=<name>` on a Hetzner source. Use `--resume` to continue and `destroy` first to re-create. `[mechanism: BootstrapExistingClusterGuard.java:73-79,121-127; BootstrapCleanup.java:414-450]`
- **Documentation corrected**: the "~15 s" halt timing, "no split-brain at any tier", a phantom `SelfDrainCoordinatorTest` citation, S19 described as a partition (it kills three of five nodes), the `durable-control-recovery.md` / `backup-recovery.md` contradictions about a consensus snapshot and whole-cluster restart, and replacement steps that cannot run without a quorum.

### Fixed (2026-10-16 — DurableProjectionRebuildTest zombie-checkpoint test raced a live consumer)
- **`zombieCheckpoint_atTheOldEpoch_isRefusedByTheApplier` was racy.** The rewind's own apply restarts the setUp
  consumer, whose async catch-up checkpoint (offset 0, rewound epoch) is accepted by the applier (same epoch,
  lower offset) and could land after the test's put of 3. Test-only: the consumer is now detached before the test
  drives the applier. [verified: with a 300 ms fixture delay on the rewound commit the old test went RED and the
  fixed test stays GREEN; `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/projection/DurableProjectionRebuildTest.java`]

### Fixed (2026-10-16 — fresh `aether cluster bootstrap` of a live cluster's name overwrote its ledger, secret and registry entry)
- **Re-running `aether cluster bootstrap` with the name of an existing cluster ran over it.** A fresh run minted a new
  secret, overwrote the live cluster's `bootstrap-state.json` and registry entry, and on Hetzner adopted its firewall, so a
  later `destroy <name>` swept the live cluster's VMs by label. `ClusterAlreadyExists` was declared and never raised.
- A fresh bootstrap (not `--resume`) now refuses before `BootstrapPhaseValidate` mints a secret and before any state is
  written when (1) the registry holds the name, (2) a local bootstrap state exists for it (an unreadable one counts), or
  (3) a cloud source's provider lists an instance labelled `aether-cluster=<name>` (first page of the label-filtered
  listing; one hit is enough). The message names the check and the way forward: `--resume`, or `destroy` first. A
  check that cannot be made (unreadable registry, provider call failing or timing out after 30 s) refuses with
  `ExistingClusterCheckFailed` instead of proceeding. There is no `--force`: an override is how the incident recurs.
  `ClusterAlreadyExists` gained a `matched` component.
  [verified: `aether/cli/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/cli/cluster/BootstrapExistingClusterGuardTest.java`]
- The guard sits outside `freshBootstrap`'s failure path on purpose: that path reaps the ledger recorded under the cluster
  name, which for a refused run is the live cluster's. [verified: `BootstrapExistingClusterGuardTest.OrchestratorEntryPoint`]
- Not changed: `--resume`, rollback, the ledger and the label sweep. Cloud sources only are asked; ssh, docker and forge
  sources have no provider listing, so for them checks 1 and 2 apply. [mechanism: `BootstrapExistingClusterGuard.cloudSources`]

- **Operator docs quoted unversioned Management API paths that return 404.** The API is served only under `/api/v1` (`ManagementRoute.API_BASE`; `management-api-versioning-spec.md` §2.2: no aliases, old `/api/...` paths 404, the only unversioned routes are the `raw(...)` carve-outs `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/repository/**`). 301 occurrences in 39 docs under `aether/docs/` and `docs/` now use the `/api/v1` form, including curl examples in the deploy guide, the scaling runbook, the TLS runbook, the TTM guide and the CLI reference; 7 `#get-api...` anchors repointed to `#get-apiv1...`. Four stale shapes were corrected against the route list (`/api/deploy/<id>/promote` is `/api/v1/deploy/promote/<id>`; `/api/blueprint` is `/api/v1/blueprints`).
- **Left as written, with reasons**: Forge's own port-8888 routes (unversioned by design), slice application routes, the versioning spec's old-to-new tables, files already carrying a Path note (#960), `aether/docs/archive/`, and `dashboard-ui-spec.md` (the dashboard code itself still calls unversioned paths, #300). Paths with no `/api/v1` route (for example `/api/aspects`, `/api/status`, `/api/undeploy`) are untouched rather than guessed. [verified: the extractor (`/api` not followed by `/v1`) finds 301 changed-class hits before and 0 after; every changed line differs from its original only by the inserted `/v1`, except the 10 hand-mapped shape corrections listed in the report; source at 4b2cc50fdb, not a build]
- **Known limitation documented: the dashboard against a real node.** `known-limitations.md` gains an entry. The dashboard calls unversioned `/api/...` over REST and the node serves `/api/v1` only, so panels fed only by REST are empty. The three WebSockets (`/ws/status`, `/ws/dashboard`, `/ws/events`) are served unversioned, so WebSocket-fed panels get data. Store by store: 5 WebSocket-fed (metrics, topology, governors, strategies, streams), 5 mixed (cluster, deployments, schema, alerts, events), 4 REST-only (requests/traces, observability depth, storage, desired topology), 1 Forge-only. Health works through `/api/v1/health`. Forge serves a subset of the dashboard's REST paths (20 distinct paths are not served there either) and feeds only `/ws/status`: its `/ws/dashboard` and `/ws/events` are `StatusWebSocketHandler`s with no publisher, so the topology, governors, strategies, streams, schema and metric-aggregate panels are empty on Forge too, and alert history and past events come only from REST. The entry also states that the node never pushes alert history (`HISTORY` answers `GET_HISTORY` only, and carries metrics history) and that `/ws/events` does not replay history on connect. What to do: use the CLI or the `/api/v1` REST endpoints. Tracked in #300 (rc6). The five docs that tell operators to open the dashboard against a real cluster point at the entry. [verified: classification read from the dashboard stores, `app.js`, `DashboardMetricsPublisher.java` and `ManagementServer.java` at the PR head; not run against a live node.; the former [unverified] points (alert HISTORY, event replay, Forge WebSocket frames, Forge write/delete route shapes) were established from `DashboardWebSocketHandler.java`, `EventWebSocketHandler.java`, `ForgeServer.java`, `ObservabilityProxyRoutes.java` and `LoadRoutes.java`.]
- **The 83 references to routes with no `/api/v1` form** were rewritten to the real route, rewritten or dropped when the route was removed or never existed, or left where deliberately historical. Forge's route table in `demos.md` was corrected to the routes `forge-api` registers. [verified: every `/api/v1` path added by the PR checked against the 200 `ManagementRoute` entries (method and shape); relative links 0 dangling by `scripts/check-md-links.py`; anchors checked in the 51 changed files with a GitHub-slug checker, 0 introduced by the PR, positive control reported a planted bad anchor; source only, no build.]

### Changed (2026-10-15 — #2201: streams and durable-entity limits stated; overclaiming documents corrected)
- **`known-limitations.md` now states the streams and durable-entity limits** until the spec-first overhaul tracked in #2201 lands: a lagging declarative consumer stalls on `CursorExpired`; sealed-tier retention is a node-wide 24 h; sealing writes one segment per evicted event; the default 128 MiB stream memory budget fits about 50 partition rings per node; production replication is not batched; a retried durable-entity `update` that missed its replication barrier applies twice; the transactional cursor path is unwired.
- **Corrections to earlier changelog entries** (those entries are history and stay as published):
  - The durable-entity timers entry (#351) said a timer survives "the whole cluster restarting". It survives a node restart and an owner handover; a whole-cluster restart restores from `[backup]`, which withholds entity checkpoints, so entity state, timers included, restarts empty (`BackupRestoreCoordinator.warnEntityCheckpointsNotRestored`, `operators/runbooks/backup-recovery.md`).
  - The Phase 1 "Transactional cursor commits ... exactly-once semantics" entry: `PgTransactionalCursorCommit` has no production caller, so no stream path is exactly-once.
  - The Phase 1 "Batch replication" entry: the node builds the non-batching `ReplicationManager.replicationManager`; `batchingReplicationManager` has no production caller.
  - The Phase 1 "Consumer group coordination" entry: join/leave writes `ConsumerGroupKey` records that no read consults, and the status response lists members, not partitions.
- **Documentation corrected to match:** a topic `idempotencyKey` sets the message ID and does not deduplicate on publish; feature-catalog row 138 is now Partial; the management API and CLI consumer-group examples no longer show partitions. `[mechanism: each correction cites the code in known-limitations.md and guarantees-corrections-needed.md D22-D26]`

### Fixed (2026-10-15 — EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest read an auto-heal replacement's vote as a refused process's)
- **`relaunchedSameIdentityProcess_*_neverRestoresQuorum` was racy, not the boot-token gate.** When the leader's first reconcile pass saw the full membership before the early kill of `btk-3`, auto-heal provisioned a fresh-NodeId core 15 s later, and that core plus `btk-1` committed the post-kill write the test reads as "a refused process voted". The test now blocks provisioning (`withComputeProviderDecorator`) and asserts the live set and the survivor's MEMBER records are exactly the expected electorate before the `btk-2` kill; the heal arm gets the same. `[verified: aether/ember/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/ember/EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest.java]` The old test goes RED with an 8 s pause before the kill (forced auto-heal); the new test stays GREEN under the same pause with the refused-provision counter positive; with `BootTokens.admit` always admitting, the new test goes RED (the refused process never exits).
- **The class's other reds were harness defects too.** Its private scan of four 23000-23300 blocks (step 100) overlapped through SWIM's UDP at the QUIC port + 100, so a live or leaked cluster poisoned its neighbour and the candidates ran out ("no free port block ... after 90000 ms", 2 of 5 runs failed on an idle box); it now uses the shared probed pool (17 candidates). `coreKilledWhileForming...` failed whenever its two repetitions both missed the race; it now attempts the scenario up to 14 times (miss probability 0.5^14 = 6.1e-5) and fails only on a wrong outcome or on never reaching it. `[verified: EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest, 6 consecutive green runs]` The sockets that stay bound after a refused or force-killed node are a separate lifecycle defect, not fixed here.
- **`EmberCluster` teardown stops what it clears (harness leak).** A node that `relaunchNode` or auto-heal added while an abort or a stop was already in flight was not in the teardown's snapshot, so `nodes.clear()` dropped it unstopped and its QUIC, management and app-HTTP sockets stayed bound until the JVM exited. Abort, failed-start and `stop()` now also stop every node the registry gained after their snapshot. `[verified: EmberClusterTeardownWiringTest#abortStart_stopsANodeAddedWhileItsStopsAreInFlight, #stop_stopsANodeAddedWhileItsStopsAreInFlight]` RED before, GREEN after. The forming-kill test now kills `btk-3` when `btk-1` reports it connected, not on a clock; the blind early kill can miss the race (the original is never seen), and whether it misses every attempt depends on the box (it reached the refusal in 4 of 4 verifier runs on a loaded Mac, through the 14-attempt retry loop, which is what makes the test robust). The demotion assertions (`awaitDemoted`, `requireElectorate`) now require the killed original to LEAVE the survivor's effective set (DEPARTING or DEAD), not merely stop being MEMBER: a link eviction moves it to SUSPECT, which still votes in the count. `[verified: EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest#coreKilledWhileForming_andSupersededByTheSameNodeId_isDemotedOnTheSurvivor]` RED with #2173's SwimProtocol fix reverted.

### Fixed (2026-10-15 — SWIM stop-before-start left a zombie detector bound to its UDP port)
- **A `stop()` that reached the SWIM health detector before its first `start()` was lost.** `Stopped` is both the
  initial and the post-stop state and ignored `StopRequested`, so the later `StartRequested` moved to `Starting`,
  bound the SWIM UDP port, reached `Running` and nothing ever stopped it. It bites in-JVM hosts (Forge, Ember);
  under `Main` process exit releases the socket.
- The early stop is now terminal: `Stopped` carries a `closed` latch, a stop of an open `Stopped` closes it, and a
  later `StartRequested` is refused with a WARN. A late `ProtocolReady` from an already-launched start is still
  closed as an orphan (#1308). Stopping a Running or Starting detector lands in the open `Stopped`, so ordinary
  stop/start restart is unchanged; the only production start site is `AetherNode.startSwim`.
  [verified: `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/health/CoreSwimHealthDetectorStartLeakTest.java`,
  `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/health/fsm/SwimHealthFsmTest.java`]
- `CoreSwimHealthDetector.start()` short-circuits on a closed detector: no transport is built, no port is bound, and
  it resolves as a logged no-op success. It deliberately does not fail: `AetherNode.startSwim` runs `failNode` on a
  start failure (production: halt; Ember: a stale one could stop a same-id relaunch). `startSwim` skips the join
  announcement when the detector is closed.
  [verified: `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/AetherNodeStartSwimTest.java`]

### Fixed (2026-10-14 — #953: the README Quick Start could not work on a clean machine)
- **The Quick Start never cloned the repository, and every example built Forge from source.** The README ran the installer and then `cd examples/pricing-engine`, a directory nothing had created; the installed Forge was never used, because each `examples/*/run-forge.sh` hardcoded `aether/forge/forge-core/target/aether-forge.jar` and built it, and the example, with `-pl … -am` from the monorepo root.
- The Quick Start is now install, clone, `cd`, start PostgreSQL, `./run-forge.sh`, and `curl` in a second terminal. It names its release once, `AETHER_VERSION=<V>`: the installer installs that release (`--version`) and the clone takes tag `v<V>`, so the tools and the examples cannot drift apart. The six `run-forge.sh` scripts share `examples/run-forge-lib.sh`, which uses `$AETHER_FORGE`, then `aether-forge` on `PATH`, then the installer's `~/.aether/bin/aether-forge` and `~/.aether/lib/aether-forge.jar`, and otherwise fails with the install command. A Forge built from the checkout is the contributor path, taken only with `--forge-from-source`. Each example now builds from its own `pom.xml`, against published artifacts only. [verified: `tools/quickstart-check.sh` against `1.0.0-rc4-candidate`]
- **New gate, `tools/quickstart-check.sh`.** It extracts the Quick Start blocks from `README.md` and runs them in a clean container (no `~/.m2`, no checkout) with a private Docker daemon for PostgreSQL. It fails unless the README's `AETHER_VERSION` equals the version of the tree under test (the root pom's, minus `-SNAPSHOT`), and it accepts the second terminal only when its output carries a numeric `totalPrice`. `--version` runs the Quick Start against a candidate, and a Maven repository can stand in for Central until the version is published there; `stage-repo` builds that repository from the publish set. Deleting the README's clone step, a wrong path in the `curl`, or a stale `AETHER_VERSION` turns it red. [verified: `tools/quickstart-check.sh`]
- **Release step: bump the Quick Start version.** When the root pom moves to a new version (the "update README.md version references" step of preparing a release branch), set `AETHER_VERSION` in the README Quick Start to it as well; `tools/quickstart-check.sh` fails on a mismatch, naming both versions.
- `aether/README.md`, the slice-developer getting-started guide, the Forge guide and the deployment guide now say that Forge comes from the installer, and label the source build as the contributor path.

### Fixed (2026-10-13 — #2184: the WebSocket aggregate size limit is pinned by a test)
- A test now pins the bound on a fragmented WebSocket message to the server's content length from both sides: exactly the limit is delivered whole, and one byte over is never delivered, closes the connection and gives the handler only `Close`. [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]

### Fixed (2026-10-13 — #2184: http-server WebSocket handlers never received events, and endpoints after the first never handshook)
- **No `WebSocketHandler` registered with `NettyHttpServer` ever received a message, and every endpoint
  after the first never completed its handshake.** Netty's handshake handler consumed the upgrade request
  before the per-channel state was stored, so `Open`, `Text`, `Binary` and `Close` were all dropped. Netty
  also installs a single handshake handler bound to the first endpoint's path, so an upgrade to the second
  or a later endpoint reached the pipeline tail and the client timed out. Aether's management server and
  Forge register three endpoints each (`/ws/dashboard`, `/ws/status`, `/ws/events`), so none of the
  dashboard's WebSocket feeds worked.
- A per-channel router now selects the endpoint by request path and installs exactly one protocol handler
  for it. The session is created on `HandshakeComplete`, so `Open` is always the first message a handler
  sees. A query string on the endpoint path is accepted.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]
- `Close` is delivered exactly once, when an opened connection goes inactive. That covers a client close
  frame, a server-side `WebSocketSession.close()`, and a connection dropped without a close frame.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]
- A fragmented message reaches the handler whole, text and binary alike, bounded by the server's content
  length; one that grows past it closes the connection undelivered. Delivering frames at all is new, so
  without aggregation the handler would have taken the first fragment for the whole message.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]
- Endpoints match the raw request path, the form Netty's handshake checks, so `/ws/%61` is refused rather
  than handed to the plain HTTP handler. An unsupported `Sec-WebSocket-Version` is answered with `426`
  before anything is installed, so a client may retry on the same connection, to any endpoint.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]
- Requests the upgrade router consumes are released; a PARANOID leak-detector test pins it.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketBufferLeakTest.java`]
- An upgrade to a path with no registered endpoint is refused with `404` and the connection is closed. It
  previously reached the plain HTTP handler.
  [verified: `integrations/net/http-server/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/http/server/WebSocketEndpointTest.java`]
- Through a real socket, a management server's `/ws/status` now delivers its status broadcast, and
  `/ws/events` prompts for authentication on open.
  [verified: `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/api/ManagementServerWebSocketFeedsTest.java`]

### Fixed (2026-10-13 — #2181: postgres-async swapped SQLSTATE and severity in every server error)

- **`ErrorResponse.asServerResponse()` passed severity where `SqlError.ServerResponse` expects the
  SQLSTATE.** The record is `(code, level, message)`; it was built as `(level, code, message)`, so
  `response().code()` returned `ERROR`/`FATAL` and `level()` returned the SQLSTATE for every error
  that arrived from the wire. Three consumers read the wrong field:
  the prepared-statement recovery in `PgConnection` (keyed on `42P05`/`26000`) never ran;
  `ServerConnectionException` and `ServerErrorOperatorIntervention` never classified a server-sent
  error as transient, so the retry policy never retried `08001`/`08004`/`08006` or `57P01`–`57P03`;
  and `ServerError.message()` printed `23505: SQLSTATE=ERROR`. The choice of error class was not
  affected: `PgProtocolStream.toSqlError` keys its mapper on `ErrorResponse.code()`, which the wire
  decoder fills correctly (`S` → severity, `C` → SQLSTATE).
- **Pinned through the wire mapping.** `ErrorResponseWireMappingTest` decodes ErrorResponse bytes with
  the real `ErrorResponseDecoder`, then checks `code`/`level`/`message`, the rendered message, transient
  classification for `08006` and `57P01`, and the stale-statement predicate for `42P05`/`26000` (and
  not for `23505`); all five tests are red with the old argument order. `ServerErrorWireTest`
  (Testcontainers) provokes a real unique violation and asserts `code() == "23505"`, and drops a
  cached statement with `DEALLOCATE ALL` to show the recovery now re-prepares and returns the row.
  `PgConnection.isStaleStatementError` is package-private so the predicate can be tested directly.

### Fixed (2026-10-12 - a killed core superseded by its NodeId stayed MEMBER on the survivor, #2173)
- **A core that was killed before the survivors' QUIC link to it was up, and whose NodeId a new process then took over, stayed `Member` in the survivor's membership FSM indefinitely.** The original's link close was never observed; the takeover was retired by a boot-token conflict, which is a death-path removal and by design feeds the FSM no liveness-gone; the SWIM FAULTY was turned into UNKNOWN by the cold-boot rule and then dropped when the member was swept. A `Member` has no presence-down exit, so the dead identity kept counting in effective membership, slice and stream placement, and the replacement deficit. A retirement is now positive evidence of death: SWIM emits the FAULTY/DEPARTED pair at once, past the cold-boot suppression, the transport veto and the co-confirmation gate, including for a member already FAULTY whose edge had been deferred. It follows only a boot-token conflict proven by the member's own answer, never a partition heal, which keeps the process's token. Separately, a cold-boot-deferred death whose member the residency sweep removes before the convergence window closes is no longer dropped: it is replayed when the gate closes (or on an identity refutation) unless the peer came back. Only the latest sweep's deferral is kept, and none for a peer that proved itself HEALTHY after its edge was deferred, so a peer that came back and died again is not departed a second time; a retired identity's death is emitted once per identity. The sweep itself is unchanged, and a slow seed stays re-addable while the gate is shut; a seed still absent when the gate closes is now departed and tombstoned by the replay. [verified: `SwimRetiredIdentityDeathTest` (14 cases: cold boot, the formed-cluster shape past the co-confirmation gate, the transport veto, exactly-once, the cluster-wide `PeerObservedFaulty`, and the swept-deferral edge cases); reverting either part, or any guard named here, turns its tests red; `EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest.coreKilledWhileFormingAndSupersededByTheSameNodeId_isDemotedOnTheSurvivor`, which skips a repetition whose relaunch was admitted as a first process and fails when no repetition reached the scenario; the cold-boot, refutation, tombstone and boot-token suites stay green]

### Fixed (2026-10-12 — #2167: `RabiaEngineSlowApplyDiagnosticsTest` red in CI when the stack sample landed in a lambda bootstrap)
- **Test race, no production change.** The blocking task counted its latch down and then reached a lambda call site; on a cold, loaded JVM the first lambda spends seconds in class generation, so a sample taken then showed the JDK's bootstrap frames instead of the blocking call (CI run 38189775550). The tests now wait until the worker is parked inside the blocking call (a direct `await`, no lambda) before sampling, and the watchdog test pins only the report's shape. `SlowTaskProbe` itself is unchanged: a task that spends a second in a lambda bootstrap IS a slow task and is reported with that stack. `[verified: RabiaEngineSlowApplyDiagnosticsTest]`

### Fixed (2026-10-12 - `EmberSameIdentityRelaunchTest` window opened 120 s late and read the killed original's membership record)
- **`relaunchedSameIdentityProcess_*` could fail on any PR with "the survivor re-admitted the refused identity as a member during the window" (#2165, run 38189775550).** The test waited for the relaunched process's start promise, which never resolves for a refused process, so the readmission window always opened `START_BOUND` = 120 s after the relaunch. Its first sample then read the survivor's membership record for the NodeId, which belongs to the killed original until the survivor registers its death; on the failing run that record still said `Member`, and no live process had been admitted (the refused process exited 0.5 s after launch). The test now waits, before the relaunch, for the survivor to register the original's death (failing with the stuck state named if it never does), then for the refused process's exit, and only then samples the 90 s window. The window therefore opens right after the refusal, about 100 s earlier, and the test runs about 100 s shorter. The product defect behind a stuck `Member` record is #2173, fixed in the same change (see that fragment). The failing run's exact interleaving (a formed cluster, no organic link close) was not reproduced, so this does not prove that run's red fixed. [unverified: the CI run's interleaving, not reproduced]

### Fixed (2026-10-12 — #2162, #2163, #2164: three node-deployment FSM defects)
- **#2162: one replica unloading no longer stops stream consumption cluster-wide.** `doUnpublishStreamSubscriptions` removed the cluster-scoped `StreamRegistrationKey` unconditionally, so a rebalance, drain or scale-down that unloaded ONE replica of a slice with a declarative `[streams.X]` consumer made every node's `StreamConsumerManager` detach it, with no error and the other replicas still ACTIVE. The removal now takes the `artifactHostedElsewhere` guard the scheduled-task unpublish already had; the last replica still removes the registration. [verified: `NodeDeploymentStateStreamGuardAndLoadChainTest.peerStillHosts_streamRegistrationSurvivesThisReplicasUnload`, with `lastReplicaUnload_removesStreamRegistrations` and `scheduledTaskUnpublish_withPeerHosting_removesNothing` as controls]
- **#2163: a consensus write failure at LOADING or LOADED no longer condemns a healthy artifact.** The exhausted retries of those two writes raised an untyped cause, which the PERMANENT disposition of `handleLoadingFailure` (#930) recorded as a fatal `UnexpectedError`, so an infrastructure stall could roll a blueprint back under `ALL_OR_NOTHING`. The two writes of the load chains (the LOAD chain and the KV-convergence redeploy) now type their failure `Intermittent.Timeout`; a genuine load failure is still fatal. The shared `updateSliceStateWithRetry` is deliberately unchanged. [verified: `loadingWriteFails_isNotFatal`, `loadedWriteFails_isNotFatal`, control `genuineLoadFailure_isStillFatal`], `redeploy_loadingWriteFails_isNotFatal` and `redeploy_loadedWriteFails_isNotFatal` for the KV-convergence redeploy chain, with control `redeploy_genuineLoadFailure_isStillFatal`
- **#2164: a slice reactivated after a quorum flap receives runtime config changes again.** Reactivation rebuilt the per-slice `ConfigNotificationManager` empty and never re-registered the slice, so later `config set` calls silently never reached a `[config-update]` slice until it was redeployed. Reactivation now runs `registerAndNotifyConfig`, so the slice also gets one initial notification per reactivation. Stream registrations and refs need no re-publication (cluster KV state and refcounts that suspension does not touch). [verified: `configChangeStillReachesSliceAfterQuorumFlap` with its in-test control; `streamRegistrationSurvivesQuorumFlap_withoutRepublish` pins the refuted arm]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — a leader change mid-replacement trimmed a healthy follower)
- **A voter is removed only on observed evidence of failure.** A freshly elected leader ranked every voter it had not yet observed as unready, so its heal could drop a healthy voter during a replacement swap and the surplus trim then drained it (`FAILED_KEPT_BOTH`). Now a voter is healed only when it was observed in a state other than READY and SYNCING (SYNCING is what a healthy follower reports across a leader change) or membership holds it Dead or Departing, and a Dead voter's stale READY entry no longer shields it; a never-observed voter is never healed away, however long the leader has led. A surplus trim (more voters than configured) is a size reduction, not a heal: it removes failed voters first, then never-observed ones, then healthy ones (id order only breaks ties), and never runs while a replacement swap is in progress. A swap's leaver is always the original. [verified: `CoreVoterReconcilerTest`, `FailedVoterEvidenceTest`, and `EmberVoterHealTest` (kill a voter in a 5-core cluster: it is replaced within the bound; emptying the evidence argument at the `AetherNode` call site turns it red)]
- **A startup config race, or an inventory initialization still in progress, defers instead of rolling back.** A replacement that began before the bootstrap source configuration was committed was rolled back with "Committed source configuration required for fleet inventory". Provisioning now waits for the configuration, bounded by the provisioning deadline, and a configuration that never appears ends the replacement with a cause naming the missing committed configuration. [verified: `NodeReplacementEnvTest`]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #2087: stream replicas served records above the acknowledged high-water)
- **A consumer could read a record that a failover then replaced at the same offset.** A replica's visible position was its own
  log end, so it served offsets the owner had not seen acknowledged (a verifier probe: acknowledged through offset 7, replica
  served 8-9). Streams are now read-committed: a record is added only when its configured acknowledgements arrive, and no
  consumer read path of the owner or of a replica returns an offset above the acknowledged high-water. The owner sends its
  visible position to its replicas (`ReplicationMessage.CommitAdvance`, new wire type, tag 2142) when it advances and repeats it
  every second; a replica serves `min(own durable, the owner's reported position)`, and nothing until the owner has reported.
  Reads above the position return an empty page, not an error. A promoted replica keeps the position it held and exposes its
  tail once its own peers acknowledge it. Replication-class reads (catch-up, survivor pulls) and the entity-log fold still read
  the appended head. The staleness bound after the last acknowledgement is one tick (1 s) plus delivery.
  `[mechanism: StreamPartitionManager.exposeReplicaCommitted bounds every replica visible advance by the owner's reported position]`
  `[verified: aether/ember/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/ember/EmberReadCommittedFailoverTest.java]`
  Per-path table: `aether/docs/reference/guarantees.md`.
- **Metadata and bounds report the committed span.** `StreamAccess.metadata()`, the partition-detail and consumers routes and the stream totals
  reported the appended head and the ring's raw count (head 1, count 2 against a visible head of -1). They now report the committed head and
  the committed count; the replication code that needs what a node HOLDS reads `appendedHead`.
  `[verified: StreamRoutesCommittedBoundsTest, ReadCommittedStreamTest]`
- **Durable-entity reads serve committed state only.** A client `get` of a key whose newest record is not yet committed waits up to the replication
  barrier timeout and then fails `NotYetCommitted` (transient); the owner's own writes and timers still sequence against pending entries, and a
  checkpoint claims only committed offsets. `[verified: EntityCommittedReadEndToEndTest]`
- **An unacknowledged tail commits without a new publish, by the existing replica re-verify.** A record an owner holds above its visible
  position (inherited at a promotion, or left by a lost acknowledgement) is acknowledged again by `PartitionBackfill`'s periodic re-verify of
  CAUGHT_UP replicas (5 s redrive, 20 s gate with the defaults: about 25 s plus a round trip); it does not run for a SYNCING, quarantined or
  unreachable replica, or on the HRW owner itself. `[verified: EmberReadCommittedFailoverTest]`
- **A divergent-tail cut invalidates the entity fold.** The fold built before a cut could keep serving (and sequencing on) a record the cut
  removed. The log counts its cuts (`StreamPartitionManager.cutGeneration`); a fold built under an older count is dropped and rebuilt from
  the surviving log, a client read waits on the rebuild or refuses `FoldInProgress`, and a stale fold is never checkpointed.
  `[verified: EntityCutInvalidatesFoldTest]`
- **The cut window and re-created streams.** The log's identity is odd from before a cut shrinks the ring until after it and carries the ring's
  incarnation: a fold built in the window is never published, a read in it refuses, and a deleted-and-created-again stream does not inherit the old
  fold; a catch-up in flight at a cut is dropped with the fold. `[verified: EntityCutInvalidatesFoldTest, EntityCommittedReadTest]`
- **A checkpoint is validated against the lineage it was taken over.** The bounded promotion escape may cut acknowledged records, and a checkpoint
  claiming one of them used to seed the rebuilt entity fold with it (the new lineage's record at that offset was never folded). A checkpoint now
  records the identity of the log record at its claim (owner epoch when known, digest of the last 8 records); seeding compares it with the local
  log and a mismatch discards the checkpoint and rebuilds from the log. The cut's generation bracket now closes on every exit, including a failed
  ring shrink. `[verified: EntityCheckpointCutTest, CutBracketTest]`
- A checkpoint with no recorded lineage (written by older code) is discarded when a fold would seed from it, and the fold is rebuilt from the log. `[verified: EntityCheckpointCutTest, EntityCommittedReadTest]`
- A checkpoint's lineage identity includes the owner epoch, and a copy that cannot supply the epoch of the claim record (it keeps no epoch history) discards the checkpoint instead of trusting a digest alone. `[verified: EntityCheckpointCutTest, EntityCommittedReadTest]`
- A checkpoint claim is accepted without validation only at or below the sealed floor its writer recorded in the checkpoint (the current floor proves nothing: it can rise over a rewritten claim); above it, a copy whose ring evicted the start of the claim's window still validates over the records it holds, and discards the checkpoint if the claim record itself is unreadable. `[verified: EntityCheckpointCutTest]`

### Changed (2026-10-11 — #1989: BSL narrowed to ten runtime modules, Apache-2.0 everywhere else, in place)
- **The licence boundary is a list, not a directory.** `tools/license/bsl-modules.txt` names the BSL 1.1 modules (`aether/node`, `aether-deployment`, `aether-control`, `aether-ttm`, `aether-ttm-onnx`, `aether-stream`, `aether-invoke`, `ember`, `forge/forge-api`, `forge/forge-core`, plus the `forge-tests` harness); everything else, the rest of `aether/`, `jbct/slice-processor*` included, is Apache-2.0. No directory moved.
- Headers, poms and LICENSE files follow the list through `tools/license/relicense.py` (idempotent: a second run changes 0 files): BUSL-1.1 headers leave the Apache modules, the BSL header sits on every `.java` file in a BSL module, each BSL module has its own `LICENSE` and declares BSL in its pom, the root pom declares Apache only, and `aether/LICENSE` and the two `jbct/slice-processor*` LICENSE files are gone.
- **A new CI gate, `tools/check-licence-closure.py`**, fails when an Apache module compile/runtime-depends on a BSL module (or has a BSL parent), when a `.java` header sits on the wrong side, or when the list and the root `LICENSE` map disagree. [verified: `tools/test_licence_closure.py`, each check mutation-probed]
- Maven Central publishes nothing from the BSL modules. [mechanism: none of the 33 published modules lies under a listed path, and check (a) of the gate refuses any dependency edge into one]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1974: an outcome write could regress a terminal, and a SUCCEEDED refused by the version fence was lost)
- **`BlueprintService.confirmOutcomeStart` retried over its own apply's terminal.** "Landed" meant "IN_PROGRESS",
  so a publish whose apply had already settled (the FSM wrote SUCCEEDED for that attempt before the
  confirmation read) was treated as fenced out, and the retry wrote IN_PROGRESS over the real outcome.
  The retry now stops when the record is IN_PROGRESS, describes this publish's own attempt, or when the committed
  blueprint belongs to another attempt (a newer publish owns the id). Only a terminal of an earlier attempt, beside
  this attempt's own blueprint, is retried over.
  Pinned by `BlueprintServiceTest$RedeployAfterPriorFailureTests` (unit, in-memory store without the version fence); [design intent — unverified] on a live cluster.
- **A SUCCEEDED outcome refused by the version fence was lost silently.** `recordSucceededOutcome` derived the
  version when the command was built and never checked it landed; a racing write of the record (a publish's
  IN_PROGRESS) made the applier drop it, and nothing revisits an apply that already left in-flight tracking.
  It now re-reads after the apply resolves and rebuilds against the current version, bounded by five attempts and
  logged at ERROR on exhaustion. It does not retry once a terminal for the attempt is committed or the id carries
  another attempt.
  Pinned by `AttemptBoundOutcomeTest.succeededOutcomeRefusedByARacingWrite_isRebuiltAgainstTheCurrentVersionAndLands`
  and `succeededOutcomeRefusedByANewerPublish_isNotRetriedOverTheNewerAttempt` (unit, real fenced `KVStore`); [design intent — unverified] on a live cluster.
- The FAILED and ROLLED_BACK terminals of an ALL_OR_NOTHING rollback were already rebuilt on a refusal by #972's
  transactional rollback; no change there. [mechanism: `submitRollback` re-invokes the command supplier, which re-derives the version]
- **The first SUCCEEDED write also respected nothing.** It was unconditional, so it could replace a newer attempt's
  FAILED when the store was ahead of the FSM, replace the same attempt's BEST_EFFORT FAILED, or write an outcome for a
  deleted blueprint. It now applies the same check as its retries. Rule per transition, for one blueprint id:
  - `IN_PROGRESS(N)` to `SUCCEEDED/FAILED/ROLLED_BACK(N)`: written.
  - A terminal for `N` to any other write for `N`: refused, with two exceptions. A BEST_EFFORT permanent failure merges
    its slices into a FAILED for `N`, and it also replaces a SUCCEEDED for `N` (a partial permanent failure reads FAILED,
    in either order). A BEST_EFFORT FAILED is the FSM's own decision that a slice is permanently failed (the operator
    was told, the artifact is no longer redeployed), not a guess written on a timeout, so a later SUCCEEDED does not erase it.
  - A write for `N` while the committed blueprint is another attempt: refused for the SUCCEEDED and the rollback writers;
    the BEST_EFFORT merge writes under the committed attempt. While the blueprint is absent (deleted during the apply):
    SUCCEEDED refused, BEST_EFFORT writes nothing, and an ALL_OR_NOTHING rollback is skipped (INFO) rather than writing a
    FAILED for the deleted id, since the deletion supersedes it.
  - A terminal for an earlier attempt `M` to `IN_PROGRESS(N)` or to `SUCCEEDED(N)`: written.
  Pinned by `AttemptBoundOutcomeTest.storeAheadOfFsm_newerAttemptsTerminal_isNotRegressedByStaleSucceeded`,
  `bestEffortFailedOwnAttempt_thenInFlightCompletes_keepsTheFailed` and `deleteWhileApplyInFlight_thenCompletes_writesNoOutcome` and `rollbackOfADeletedBlueprint_writesNoOutcomeForTheDeletedId`
  (unit, real fenced `KVStore`); [design intent — unverified] on a live cluster.

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1967: forwarded stream reads lost the typed error, so a remote owner's refusal answered 500 or was masked)
- **A stream read served by a remote owner did not fail the way a local read does.** `ReadForwardResponse` carried a refusal as text only, and the caller rebuilt it as `ReadForwardFailed`, a `StreamForwardError` that `StreamErrorStatus` cannot classify. The `CursorExpired` retry of a default read (#1921) and the 410 of an expired offset never saw their cause; a `StreamNotFound`, `PartitionOutOfRange` or not-yet-activated owner was not the 404, 400 or 503 a local read gives. On the routed GOVERNOR and NEAREST paths the caller then fell back to a local read of a ring it does not hold, so the same refusals surfaced as `PARTITION_NOT_LOCAL` (503) instead of their own status.
- **The response now carries the refusal typed.** `ReadForwardResponse` gains `refusal`, a `ReadRefusal`: a code (`ReadRefusal.Kind`) and the values the cause is built from, never a message to parse and never the cause chain. The owner puts it on the wire from the one `sendReadFailure` that already logs the chain (#2105); the caller rebuilds the same `Cause` a local read of the owner gives, so every route maps it as it maps a local refusal. The set is what a read can raise on the serving node, read off the code: `StreamNotFound`, `PartitionOutOfRange`, `PARTITION_NOT_LOCAL`, `BUFFER_CLOSED`, `CursorExpired`, `OwnerNotActivated`, `ReplicaNotVerified`, `StaleEpochRead`, `NotCurrentOwner`, `OwnerCatchupPending`, `LinearizableRoundTimeout`, `PartitionHeldNotMaterialized`, `RingIndexCorrupted`, `SealInFlight`, `SealedRangeMissing`; `EpochDiverged` keeps its own slots. `ReadRefusal.readRefusal` is an exhaustive switch over `StreamError` with no default, so a new stream error cannot be added without deciding whether a read raises it. A failure outside the set (a failed tier read, a consensus failure) still travels as text and is rebuilt as `ReadForwardFailed`.
- **"Stream partition is not owned by this node" from the target of a forward arrives as `PARTITION_NOT_LOCAL`**, the same retryable 503 a local miss is, and the forward still degrades to the local read for it, as for a timeout or a text-only failure. Every other typed refusal is returned as the owner's answer instead of being replaced by a local read that can only fail with `PARTITION_NOT_LOCAL`. [guess, marked: a transient owner refusal on a `NEAREST` read (for example `OwnerNotActivated`) is now a 503 where it used to degrade to the local read's empty page]
- **Wire change** (pre-GA, owner ruling 2026-09-16): `ReadForwardResponse` gains a trailing component, and `ReadRefusal` / `ReadRefusal.Kind` take wire tags 2140 / 2141; the wire-assignment baseline is re-recorded. A code this node does not know (a newer peer) is rebuilt as the owner's text.
- [verified: `ForwardedReadRefusalTest` (two real nodes in one JVM, every message through the production codec, one test per refusal), `ForwardedStreamReadRouteTest` (the real `STREAM_READ` and `STREAMS_EVENTS` routes over a forwarding router: default read retried, expired offset 410, out-of-range 400, not-owned 503), `ReadRefusalTest`; reverting each changed line turns a test red]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1734: durable-entity ownership converged late, or never, under a changing hosting set)
- **The leader minted entity-arc owners from whatever hosting set was committed at tick time, so every late registration was an owner change.** Registrations arrive one per node as each node provisions the slice, and an autoscaler adds and removes hosts. Each owner change is a fence bump with no readiness handoff, so a change every few seconds kept the new owner's not-held window open. `EntityOwnershipReconciler` now holds a per-keyspace settle gate on the fingerprint of the hosting set (partition count plus registered hosts that are live members). Only the reconciler changed: not the writer, not the epoch scheme, not `CommittedPartitionOwnerSource`.
- **What the gate does:**
  - Once the fingerprint has been unchanged for 2 tick intervals of time, 10 s at the 5 s tick (`SETTLE_TICKS`), owners are HRW over the set, as before.
  - While it has not settled, an arc whose committed owner is still a registered, live host keeps that owner, even if HRW now prefers a newly joined host.
  - An owner that left the members or retracted its registration is replaced at once; failover is never gated.
  - An arc with no record is minted only after the set settles, or after 6 tick intervals of time (`FIRST_MINT_CEILING_TICKS`, 30 s at the 5 s tick) without settling. The ceiling mint raises the operator warning `entity-ownership-unsettled-mint` (WARNING, subject the keyspace, message gives the number of set changes seen and the ceiling), once per unsettled run. Existing owners are never moved while unsettled.
  - [verified: aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/EntityOwnershipReconcilerTest.java, nested `SettleGate`] (unit-level, through the real ownership writer over a committing store; the Forge pin below is the live-path evidence). With the gate off (`settleTicks` 0) the same first scenario mints on the first pass, so the zero is the gate's doing.
- **Guarantee, stated precisely.** Owners converge to HRW(registered hosts that are live members) once that set has been quiet for 2 tick intervals of time. While it is not quiet, no owner changes except failover of an owner that left. A first mint is delayed by at most 6 tick intervals of time. No claim under a perpetually oscillating set, other than that unminted arcs are minted once at the ceiling and then stay put. This bounds the rate of owner changes; it does not bound write refusal and is not a readiness handoff: a moved arc's new owner can still be named before its ring is held, and its `OwnerTransitioning` window is unchanged. Both thresholds are measured on an injected monotonic clock, never counted in passes, because an event kick (retract, committed registration removal) is a pass that takes no time and counting it let three back-to-back kicks settle and mint a set that had been quiet for milliseconds. The quiet period is observed at pass granularity, so on a loaded scheduler it can stretch by up to one tick interval. [verified: `EntityOwnershipReconcilerTest.SettleGate.kicks_afterARegistration_doNotSettleTheSet`] (unit-level) The 2 and 6 are marked guesses, one constant each, no config knob.
- **Operator recovery.** None to take: the warning is informational and the state clears when the hosting set is quiet for 2 tick intervals of time. If it recurs, the cause is a hosting set that keeps changing (autoscaler flapping, a slice that provisions slowly); #1734 option (d), scale hysteresis for entity-declaring slices, is the separate remedy.
- **Docs.** `entity-ownership-unsettled-mint` is added to the code list in `aether/docs/reference/management-api.md`.

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1385: docs overclaimed the replay bound of a declarative stream consumer)
- **The replay bound after an ungraceful move holds only while the partition keeps receiving events.** The checkpoint trigger
  (1000 events or the 1 s / 500 ms interval since the last commit) is evaluated only on a delivery, so no timer starts a commit on a quiet
  partition: one whose events all land inside its first interval after attach never commits a checkpoint, and an ungraceful move replays it
  from offset 0. At-least-once is unaffected; the bound is not. The trailing commit that would earn it is still not implemented.
- The statement is now made, without the unqualified bound, in `guarantees.md` (§4 row 19 and the `stream.consume` entry), the design-versus-shipped
  note under the `streaming-spec.md` §10.2 checkpoint diagram, and the comments on `StreamConsumerManager`, `ConsumerRuntimeState.shouldCheckpoint`
  and `DurableGroupIdentity.consumerConfig`. The other places that state the bound were already corrected by #2111. Comments and documentation
  only; no behaviour change. [mechanism: `shouldCheckpoint` is reached only from `ConsumerRuntimeState.advanceCursor` -> `checkpointIfNeeded`]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1338: system streams were addressed by a name they are not created under, and were writable from a slice once that was fixed)
- **A stream engine key is now the full `namespace:stream:version` address in every namespace, `system` included.**
  `StreamEngineKey.engineKey` used to reduce a `system` address to its bare name (`cluster-events`), but the
  framework creates, publishes and consumes the system stream as `system:cluster-events:1.0.0`. Two consequences
  followed: a blueprint `External` `system:` source bound a consumer to a ring nobody writes to, and the
  Management-API reads of a system stream (`/streams/system/cluster-events/1.0.0/info`, metadata) answered
  "Stream not found". Both now resolve to the real stream. A user stream that is merely named `cluster-events` is an
  ordinary stream: it is no longer served at the system address and no longer refused as the system stream.
  [mechanism: `BlueprintPublishOwnershipTest$StreamBindings#publish_externalSystemSource_resolvesToTheNameTheSystemStreamIsCreatedUnder`
  and `SystemStreamManagementReadTest`; reverting `engineKey` turns both red]
- **System streams are READ-ONLY to blueprints, slices and the Management API** (owner ruling, #1338). A `system:`
  `External` source stays allowed (spec `event-stream-namespaces-spec.md` §6.1, §11.2) and binds read-only. Every
  write into a `system:` stream through `StreamWriteRouter` (slice `StreamAccess.publish`, `StreamPublisher`
  `publish`/`publishBatch`, the Management-API publish) or `DefaultStreamPublisher` is refused with
  `StreamError.SystemStreamWriteRefused` (HTTP `405`) unless the writer holds `SystemWriteGrant`, a package-private
  capability only `SystemStreamFactories` hands to the node's own system publisher. Before this, binding the
  stream (the fix above) would have let a slice append to the real system ring.
  [mechanism: `SystemStreamWriteGateTest`; making the refusal a no-op turns its three refusal tests red, withholding
  the grant from the system publisher turns its control red]
- **A slice never creates a `system:` stream.** Binding one that the runtime has not provisioned fails with
  `StreamNotFound` instead of minting it under a reserved name or comparing the slice's replication declaration with
  the committed one.
- **Behaviour changes.** A catalog create in the `system` namespace (`POST /streams/system/<name>/<version>`) used to mint
  a flat bare-named operator stream; it is now refused `400` as a reserved kind. A body-carried bare name equal to a
  system stream's bare name is no longer treated as the system stream (it still cannot be created, being not a catalog
  address).
- **Forwarded writes.** The same refusal sits on the owner's appends, which every publish reaches (single, batch,
  forwarded and the materialize-then-retry path). A write forwarded to a `system:` stream is refused at the owner unless
  the frame carries the sending node's system-writer claim (`PublishForward#systemWriter`, set only by a node's own
  system publisher). The guarantee is therefore: non-system callers and origin-side omissions cannot write a system
  stream. It is not a defence against a peer that holds the cluster secret, which can forge the claim (pinned by
  `SystemStreamForwardPinsTest#honestyPin_aPeerThatSetsTheMark_landsASystemWrite_theClaimIsForgeable`).
- **A writing role on a `system` External source is refused at deploy** (rule `source-system-not-consumer`, gating),
  instead of at the first publish. `role = "producer"` or `"both"` is refused; `consumer` or no role is accepted.

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1117: stream-consumer slices stall in ACTIVATING/ROUTING until the 30/90 s node timers force ACTIVE)
- **The stuck-slice timers wrote ACTIVE over a committed ACTIVE.** The ROUTING (30 s) and ACTIVATING (90 s) remediation read only the node's local view, which moves only when the node's own apply delivers its notification, and wrote a bare ACTIVE put. They now read this node's own `NodeArtifactKey` from its APPLIED mirror (not a consensus read) first: ACTIVE is adopted into local state with no write; a value EARLIER in the activation chain (LOAD..ROUTING) re-drives the chain's FULL last write (ACTIVE with its endpoints and the stream-ref commands, one batch) while a committed target still names the version; DEACTIVATE, DEACTIVATING, FAILED, UNLOAD, UNLOADING, UNKNOWN or no entry is adopted (an absent entry is handled as a removal) and ACTIVE is never written over it. Every remediation line names the node, the local state and the committed state. `[verified: NodeDeploymentStateStuckReconcileTest]` The re-drive builds its stream-ref Puts from the current applied mirror; if the lost original also lands late the instance holds one reference too many and the stream outlives its holders (a leak, the safe direction; per-holder reference entries are the rc5 fix). Not repaired: a committed ACTIVE written earlier by the old bare remediation stays without stream refs.
- **"Blueprint fully deployed — all N slices active" overclaimed.** It is logged on the first ACTIVE instance of each slice and says nothing about the others. The line now reads "deployed: each of its N slices has at least one ACTIVE instance [slice: n of m instances ACTIVE]; other instances may still be activating". The SUCCEEDED outcome record carries no text and has the same meaning (at least one ACTIVE instance per slice, at the leader's last apply). `[verified: DeployedVerdictTest]`
- **Not fixed here:** why the node's last write is sometimes never answered for 30/90 s after a leader change. Three logs show a ten-second stall on the new leader's consensus worker followed by an unanswered submission; the mechanism is tracked in #2143. `[design intent - unverified]`

### Added (2026-10-11 — #1117: consensus stall diagnostics)
- **Consensus pending-batch age and apply timeouts on the existing metrics surface.** `consensus_oldest_pending_batch_age_ms` (a level, 0 when nothing is pending; counted from this node's local receipt of the batch, never from the originator's stamp) and `consensus_apply_timeouts_total` on the Prometheus gauges, and `oldestPendingBatchAgeMs` / `applyTimeoutCount` in the comprehensive response's `consensus` block. No new route. `[verified: RabiaMetricsCollectorTest, RabiaEngineSlowApplyDiagnosticsTest]`
- **`SLOW-APPLY-RUNNING` names the call holding the consensus worker.** `SLOW-APPLY` is logged when a task finishes; a task still running after one second now has its worker's stack logged once, while it runs. `[verified: RabiaEngineSlowApplyDiagnosticsTest]`

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1111: a replacement the leader gives up on is terminated, not orphaned)
- **Every drop of an in-flight auto-heal replacement now reaps its instance.** `LeaderReconciler` dropped an entry at the per-source replacement
  ceiling, after twelve absent listings, on a FAILED provider report, and when the create failed, and in each case only logged at INFO: the paid
  instance stayed running on a stable leader until the next leadership change. Each drop now calls
  `ClusterTopologyManager.reapDroppedReplacement(node, reason, knowledge)`, which looks the instance up by its node-id label at the source the create
  went to, WARNs with the source, the node id and the instance id(s), and terminates it through the confirmed reap built for retirements (#2062):
  list, terminate, re-list, retried 12 times and bounded.
- **Operator-visible.** A termination that cannot be confirmed ends in the same `instance-termination-unconfirmed` mark and event as a retirement
  (recovery: `instance-termination-confirmed`). A lookup that cannot be answered is never read as "absent": it is retried and ends in that event.
- **A failed create is reaped unless the cause PROVES no instance was made.** The providers report a readiness timeout, a 5xx after the provider
  accepted, a lost response and a failed tag step as ordinary provision failures while the instance exists and bills, so only a capacity refusal
  (`CapacityUnavailable`: Hetzner `resource_unavailable`, AWS `InsufficientInstanceCapacity`, and every configured zone refusing), the fleet cap
  (`NodeCapExceeded`) and a refused fleet reservation (`CapacityControlledLifecycle.AdmissionFailure`) skip the lookup. Every other failure is looked
  up; if `12` consecutive successful listings show no instance (the absent-listing count of #1049), the drop is confirmed absent: an INFO line, no mark and no event.
- **The readiness timeout keeps its type.** `createFrom` of Hetzner, AWS, GCP, Azure and Docker flattened `ProvisionReadinessTimeout` into
  `ProvisionFailed`; each now passes it through (the instance exists).
- **Two bounds on a failed create's lookup.** It is confirmed absent only by 12 consecutive successful empty listings spaced
  `provisioningTimeout/6` apart (about 110 s at the defaults): an instance first listed later than that is not reaped by this path and is left to
  the next leader activation's orphan replay. A listing that FAILS is neither absent nor terminal: it is retried, and only 12 consecutive failures
  end in `instance-termination-unconfirmed`; any answer resets that count.
- **A joined replacement is never terminated.** Membership clears the entry of a replacement that joined, so it is never dropped; and a dropped node
  that shows life when the reap runs is deferred, as a retirement is. A replacement alive in SWIM but not yet joined when its ceiling or readiness bound
  expires is given up on by design.
- **What "confirmed" means.** An empty listing is gone only for an instance the provider listed before; twelve empty listings of an instance a create
  returned but no listing ever showed do not confirm (a listing lags creation and omits what it cannot attribute): that drop ends in
  `instance-termination-unconfirmed` with the "never listed" text, asking the operator to verify at the provider. A create that was deferred (circuit
  open, no healthy peers) made no instance and reaps nothing.
- [verified: `LeaderReconcilerTest$RealCreatePath` (the reconciler on the real topology manager and lifecycle over a fake provider whose create makes an
  instance and then fails: readiness timeout, 5xx after accept, tag failure are terminated; capacity refusal is never looked up; a create that made
  nothing is confirmed absent with no event), `ClusterTopologyManagerDroppedReplacementTest`, `LeaderReconcilerTest$InFlightInstanceState`, and one
  `createFrom` readiness test per provider asserting the typed cause.] [unverified: a real cloud run; a provider's transport timeout shapes were not
  enumerated, they are treated as ambiguous and looked up.]

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #1109: the leader issued LOAD from its mirror before the target put had committed)
- **The leader allocated from `blueprints`, a mirror written when the target put is only queued.** `handleAppBlueprintChange` writes the mirror
  and queues the `SliceTargetKey` put; the next `reconcile()` tick allocated from the mirror and issued LOAD. Pending batches are ordered by
  hash, not by submission, so that LOAD could commit ahead of the put it depends on on every replica, the leader included. Measured on the
  rc4 tip by `ClusterDeploymentStateActiveTest$LeaderLoadWaitsForCommittedTarget` (red before this change). The premise of the ticket (a
  side channel not ordered behind the put) is not what happens: LOAD is an ordinary consensus put, and a follower applies strictly by slot
  (`RabiaEngineApplyOrderTest`, `KVStoreCommittedNotificationTest` pin that half and were green).
- **`SliceAllocationEngine.tryAllocate` now issues LOAD only when the leader's applied store holds a `SliceTarget` (or a `VersionRouting`
  entry) naming the version** (`CommittedSliceTarget.permits`, the predicate ACTIVATE, the node gate and the orphan sweep already use). The check
  precedes the `sliceStates` bookkeeping: a refused attempt leaves no trace, so the target put's own notification and every later tick re-attempt it.
  `[verified: ClusterDeploymentStateActiveTest$LeaderLoadWaitsForCommittedTarget]`
- **The gate moved the stall from the node to the leader, so the visibility and the cure moved with it.** A target put that is lost (a failed
  consensus batch, a leader change) used to be loud: the LOAD went out and the node parked it and warned. With the gate it left the leader
  refusing LOAD with no signal and no retry (probe: 360 reconcile ticks, 0 LOADs, one queued put, nothing raised). Once a slice has been refused for
  the bound (2 minutes on the node clock, `ClusterDeploymentContext.setAwaitedTargetBound`), the leader raises `slice-start-awaiting-target`
  (subject `<artifact>@leader`, the message names the slice, version and duration) and re-submits the target put while the blueprint is still desired
  and no committed target names the version. Both happen at most once per bound, so a lost put costs one extra idempotent put per bound. The
  recovery `slice-start-deferral-ended` follows when the target commits or the blueprint is no longer desired. The sink is bound by `AetherNode`
  `[unverified: no test reaches the AetherNode wiring line]`.
  `[verified: ClusterDeploymentStateActiveTest$LostTargetPut]`
- **Guarantee per operation.**
  - *LOAD (leader):* issued only if, at the moment of the check, the leader's applied store names the version. Earned by the check against the
    leader's own `KVStore`. A lost target put is reported and re-submitted past the bound, not repaired instantly; between bounds the slice has no instance. Not guaranteed: that the target is unchanged when the LOAD commits (check-then-act; a rollback in between is still
    refused by the node-side gate, #1068), and not fenced against a deposed leader's plain put (H2, filed for rc5 with an exact-value guard).
  - *LOAD/ACTIVATE (node):* unchanged. A node starts a slice only when its own applied store names the version, otherwise the start is parked and
    re-driven when the target arrives (#1083).
  - *ACTIVATE (leader), UNLOAD, DEACTIVATE, DRAIN-by-ping:* unchanged.
  - Never claimed: exactly-once, or that a follower "has seen" a put on any basis other than slot order.

### Added (2026-10-11 — #1109: a start parked for a target that never arrives was silent after one WARN)
- **A LOAD, ACTIVATE or ACTIVE claim a node parked for want of a committed target now raises the operator warning
  `slice-start-awaiting-target` (WARNING) once it has stayed parked for the bound** (2 minutes, LOADING's own bound, measured on the node's
  clock from the first refusal; `NodeDeploymentContext.setParkedStartBound`). `SliceState.LOAD` has no timeout, so the leader's stuck-transitional sweep
  never sees a parked LOAD and nothing else reported it. Subject `<artifact>@<node>`.
- **The park stays retry-able**: nothing is written, failed or unloaded. The next target or routing put for the base re-drives it as before (#1083).
- **Its recovery `slice-start-deferral-ended` (INFO)** is raised when a warned park ends (target arrived, or the entry was superseded, removed or dropped as
  stale), once, for the same subject; a park that ended before the bound raises nothing. Raised once per park, never per tick.
  `[verified: NodeDeploymentStateRollbackOrphanTest$ParkedStartEscalates]` (the one-millisecond-short arm stays silent).
- Guarantee: the event reports a start held past the bound on a node that is up; delivery is best-effort like every per-node event, and the
  log line is always written. A node that is down or partitioned reports nothing.

### Fixed (2026-10-11 — #697: `[cache.*]` sections sharing a `cache_name` could silently disagree about the one backend they share)
- **Sections that share a `cache_name` share ONE backend, built from whichever section provisioned first; the others' mode, TTL and capacity were silently ignored, and a different key or value type polluted the shared heap.** The factory now refuses a later section whose `mode`, `ttl_seconds`, `max_entries` or key type differs, or whose stored value type differs (for strategies that store: not `WRITE_AROUND`, whose return type is never cached). The failure names the cache name, the differing setting and both values, surfaced under the refused section by the resource provider. The check runs inside the per-name atomic registry update, and a refused section counts no hold.
- **Sharing a `cache_name` is still allowed and still intended** (the banking example's `CACHE_ASIDE` reader and `WRITE_AROUND` invalidators); `strategy` may differ. The issue's original ask, refusing every duplicate, would have refused that example, so it was narrowed to disagreement.
  [verified: `CacheNameSharingTest`, each check with a mutation going red]
- **Types are checked only where they are known, and order does not matter.** Key and cached value types are compared only between sections whose slice factory supplied `[key, response]` type tokens, the value type only between sections whose strategy stores the result (not `WRITE_AROUND`). The type a name is held to is the first such typed section's, whatever was provisioned before it (an untyped or `WRITE_AROUND` section neither sets nor clears the recorded VALUE type; a `WRITE_AROUND` section that carries a key token does set the key type). A section without type tokens, for example the banking `getBalance` (a single `@Key` parameter), is not checked on type: `[unverified: not detectable at provisioning]`. The first section is not named in the message (the factory does not receive section names).

### Fixed (2026-10-10 — HTTP error path leaked the failure's cause chain to clients, and never logged it)
- **A failure wrapper's origin chain could reach the client, and no operator could see it.** `HttpError.message()` and a composite's `message()` walk the origin chain; the problem-body fallback, the `ProblemDetail` detail, the management plane's `ProblemResponses.writeProblem(Cause)` and several other client-body producers rendered them directly. Client bodies now render causes through one renderer, `HttpError.clientMessage(Cause)`; the chain goes to the server log only (the slice-error log line carries it in full). Shapes covered: a plain chained cause, an `HttpError` over an `HttpError`, a composite of chained `HttpError`s, a composite inside an `HttpError`, and an `HttpError` inside a composite. `HttpError.clientMessage()` defaults to the status text, so a new implementer cannot leak by omission. Inter-node error replies (invocation, forwarded HTTP and management requests, stream publish/read forwards, entity forwards) are rendered by the callee through the same renderer, so the calling node never receives, and never echoes, the chain; the callee logs the full chain locally under the same request/correlation ids. A source-scan test fails if a client-body producer renders `cause.message()` directly. [verified: `CauseShapeClientBodyMatrixTest`, `ClientBodyProducersUseRendererTest`, `SliceRouterCauseChainLeakTest`, `ProblemResponsesChainTest`, `CrossNodeCauseChainLeakTest`, `HttpErrorClientMessageTest`; reverting each changed line turns a test red]

### Fixed (2026-10-10 — #2089: a docker-source `aether cluster bootstrap` never formed quorum)
- **Docker nodes were created with an empty `PEERS`.** `DockerComputeProvider` passes `PEERS=ctx.peers().or("")`, bootstrap supplied no peers for a docker source, and nothing pushes peers afterwards, so every node fell back to the peer list baked into the image, which never contained the node's freshly minted id; each aborted at boot with `Self node ... must be in coreNodes` and bootstrap failed at cluster formation with `0/N nodes healthy`. Bootstrap now mints every core node id before provisioning and creates every node of the docker source with the same full `id:host:port` list of the cores (a container's host is its name, which is its node id; port `6000`, the docker provider's default). Workers and spots get the same core list and let the provider mint their ids. The scale-wave docker path and `DockerComputeProvider` are unchanged. [verified: `DockerBootstrapPeersTest`]
- **A docker source that declares management TLS is now refused up front, instead of failing later.** `[operations.tls] auto_generate` defaults to true, and a docker node (created by `docker run` from the image's baked plain-HTTP configuration, with no channel for TLS material) cannot honour it. The VALIDATE phase now refuses such a config with `DockerSourceDeclaresTls`, naming the fix (`[operations.tls] auto_generate = false`), before any container exists. HTTP is used only when the config explicitly disables TLS, never inferred from the source type. `aether cluster init` for a docker target now writes `auto_generate = false` explicitly. Docker nodes serving TLS is a separate, later feature. [verified: `DockerTlsRefusalTest`, `ClusterConfigGeneratorTest`]
- **Several docker sources no longer form several clusters.** Every docker core now receives ONE list naming ALL cores of ALL docker sources (`DockerCores`), and a docker worker-only source gets the same core list. A cluster with ANY docker source must have ALL its sources docker: docker nodes reach each other by container name and the others by address, so no single peer list serves a mix (cores would split, and workers of either kind would boot with a core list they cannot reach), and bootstrap refuses any mix with `DockerCoresMixedWithOtherCores` instead of splitting it. The cluster port in the list is handed to the provider explicitly (`cluster_port`), so the two cannot drift. [verified: `DockerBootstrapProvisionPhaseTest`, `DockerTlsRefusalTest`]
- **The CLI could not reach the docker nodes it had created.** A docker node's collected address was its container name (`name:8080`), which does not resolve outside the docker network, so the formation health probe timed out with `Quorum not established: 0/1 nodes healthy` on a cluster that had formed. The docker provider is now told to publish each node's management port (`expose_host_ports`, existing), bootstrap reads the mapped host port back with `docker port`, and the node's address is `127.0.0.1:<mapped port>`. Host ports work on Linux and Docker Desktop alike. `NodeAddress` and `ProvisionedNode` carry that per-node port (absent for cloud and ssh nodes, which keep the configured management port); the formation health and quorum probes, the stored management endpoint and the registered cluster endpoint use it, and a resumed run reads it back from the state file. Inter-node `PEERS` stay container names. [verified: `DockerHostReachabilityTest`]
- **Docker nodes booted with a different cluster secret than the one the CLI authenticated with.** The CLI mints (or resumes) its own cluster secret and derives its bootstrap admin key from it; cloud nodes receive that secret in their user-data, but a docker node received only whatever `AETHER_CLUSTER_SECRET` the provider forwarded from the CLI's own environment (nothing, or an unrelated value). Every node then answered the CLI's quorum probe with "Invalid API key" and `--wait` ran to its timeout on a healthy cluster. Bootstrap now builds the docker provider with a host environment that answers `AETHER_CLUSTER_SECRET` from `ctx.clusterSecret()` and every other name from the process environment, so the secret the CLI holds is the only one a docker node receives. An `AETHER_CLUSTER_SECRET` in the operator's shell is ignored for bootstrap. No operator step is added. [verified: `DockerBootstrapSecretTest`]
- `aether cluster destroy` on a docker cluster now reaches the nodes through their published host ports (serving node identified by the endpoint's published port; sibling fallback uses each recorded `host:port` as is), and no longer reports success with exit 0 over failed drain/shutdown operations: it refuses before deleting anything and names `--force-undrained`, which proceeds and lists the nodes that were not drained.
- `docker port` is consulted at destroy only for a cluster whose bootstrap ledger records docker containers, never merely because the endpoint is on loopback. IPv6 hosts are bracketed in the persisted `host:port` form (`[::1]:38915`) and parsed back; a bare IPv6 address carries no port.
- The refusal over failed drain/shutdown operations applies to every provider, cloud included, and means REAL failures (unreachable node, timeout, 5xx, any refusal other than the budget): `--force-undrained` is the operator's explicit acknowledgement that VMs may be deleted undrained.
- A drain or shutdown refused by the cluster's disruption budget (HTTP 409 "Disruption budget exceeded") is no longer a failure: a destroy can never drain a majority of the cores, so those cores are reported as held for quorum, are not shut down, and are removed with their VMs. The summary prints `drained N, held for quorum M (names), failed K`; exit 0 when K is 0. The budget is recognised by status 409 plus its exact phrase, because the response carries no structured code.
- `aether cluster bootstrap --wait --timeout N` now caps node-health and quorum-formation waits at N seconds too (never raising them above the config), instead of bounding only the final status poll. The cap is a runtime setting and never enters the hashed config, so a timed-out bootstrap can be resumed with a longer `--timeout` or none; without `--timeout`, those waits use `[operations.timeouts]` as before. The refusal message no longer ends with a stray `; .`.
- `aether cluster destroy` reconciles the cluster's node list against the nodes recorded in the bootstrap ledger. A node the cluster did not list (the lifecycle list is the leader's view of its peers and can omit one) is named as "not listed by the cluster — removed without drain" (docker nodes by container name; otherwise counted with the ledger's labels), and the summary counts drained + held + failed + not listed against the ledger total. An unlisted node alone does not refuse the destroy.

### Fixed (2026-10-10 — #2086: the divergent-tail cut reads the head inside the append lock)
- **The recovery segment and the truncation witness could miss a record the cut removed.** `StreamPartitionManager.cutRing` read the ring's head before it entered the ring's ordered section; an append that landed between that read and the lock was removed by the cut but was in neither the segment nor the witness, and the reported count and range were short. (The quarantine fence for replicated appends is enforced inside the lock, so only an owner-local append can land there.) The head is now read inside the section, once, for the witness, the segment and the report, and the reported last offset is the one actually cut. `[verified: aether/aether-stream/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/stream/StreamPartitionManagerDivergentTailTest.java]`
- Pinned the stream-name filter of the destroy-path close of a standing `stream-divergent-tail-cut-refused`: destroying one stream leaves another stream's standing warning open.

### Added (2026-10-10 — #2062: operator clear path for an unconfirmed-termination mark)

- **An operator can clear an unconfirmed-termination mark (#2062).** `aether cluster clear-unconfirmed <node> --instance <provider-instance-id|unknown> [--force]`
  (`POST /api/v1/nodes/unconfirmed/clear/{id}`, OPERATOR, leader-routed) clears ONE mark after the operator verified at the provider and terminated the instance
  by hand. The cluster asks the node's provider first, twice: by the node's labels (so a wrong or `unknown` instance id does not hide a listed instance) and,
  for a given id, by that id (so an instance shown without the node's labels is not missed). The clear is refused (409, naming the instance and its state) while
  either shows an instance that is not terminated, and refused when either read fails; an external node, which has no provider to ask, is refused with a cause that
  says so. `--force` overrides all of these and is recorded in the event. It is also refused, with nothing cleared, for a node that shows life (409), for a node with no mark
  (404), and when the mark changed while the clear was committing (the delete carries the exact mark it read, so a later incarnation's mark survives). A clear
  raises `instance-termination-cleared`, which names the node, the authenticated operator, the instance the operator attests, whether the check was forced, the
  provider state seen, the instance id the cluster had listed for the node (or `never listed`) and the mark's cause, and closes the open warning cluster-wide.
