  callback is invoked with its own facade.
- **The chain.** `DynamicConfigManager` reports each committed `ConfigKey` put/remove it honours (cluster-wide,
  or scoped to this node) to its applied-listeners AFTER updating the overlay provider —
  `AetherNode.collectRouteEntries` registers `NodeDeploymentManager::onConfigChanged`, which dispatches a
  `ConfigChanged(key)` FSM event; `Active` pushes it through `notifyChange(key, this::buildConfigFacade)`; the
  manager invokes the generated method once per (registered slice, declared section) where the section
  prefixes the dotted key, with THAT slice's facade. `notifyChange`'s old shape — one section, one facade for
  every slice — could not have been correct (each slice reads through its own composite), so it now takes the
  key and a per-artifact facade function; registrations carry their sections. Every other FSM state ignores the
  event (slices re-read at the next activation). The dead `lastParsedConfig` map is gone.
  [verified: `ConfigChangePushLivenessTest` (dead-surface gate, bytecode reachability over every module's
  `target/classes`) — red at the base with `notifyChange` unreachable; red again with the one `AetherNode` line
  removed (`onConfigChanged`/`onApplied` unreachable); `ConfigNotificationManagerChangeTest` — two slices with
  sections `database`,`cache` / `database.pool`, key `database.pool.size` reaches both with their own facades,
  `databases.other` and `cache.ttl` reach nobody (red with the prefix test forced true; red with a shared
  facade); `NodeDeploymentFsmTest#active_ConfigChanged_isPushedToTheRegisteredSlice` (red with the `case`
  removed) and `#dormant_ConfigChanged_isIgnored`; `DynamicConfigManagerAppliedListenerTest` — the listener
  sees the overlay already updated for put and remove, and a key scoped to another node is neither applied nor
  reported (red with the put-side notify removed)]
- **Guarantee, precisely** (`guarantees.md` §C4 / row 25, catalog row 176): process-local per node,
  asynchronous on the notification thread, at-most-once per change per (slice, section) — a callback that
  throws is logged, never retried — and only while the node is ACTIVE. The `DeadSurfaceCommissioningTest`
  positive control that asserted `notifyChange` dead is retired (the permanent gate is coupled to its synthetic
  fixture, not to #381, per its own doc).
- [unverified: no boot test deploys a slice with a `@ConfigUpdate` method and issues `config set` — the
  end-to-end path is pinned structurally (reachability) plus three behavioural pins on its three segments,
  not observed on a running node; the generated `notifyConfigUpdate`'s own parse-and-dispatch is unchanged
  and untested here.]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #311: `cluster init` was overwrite-or-abort against an existing config)
- **Re-running `cluster init` against an existing output aborted a batch run (`OutputExists`, now
  removed — no path returns it) and, with `--force`, replaced the file wholesale** — a hand-added section or a tuned value was either
  a blocker or a casualty, so the generator could not be re-run to change one answer. Without
  `--force` the generated config is now **merged into the existing file in place**
  (`InPlaceTomlMerge`): the parsers only LOCATE and COMPARE, and the text written is the operator's
  text with exactly these edits — a generated key whose parsed value differs is rewritten on its own
  line (value only; key spelling and trailing comment kept), a generated key or section the file
  lacks is appended into place, and every other line — comments, blank lines, section order, value
  spelling, hand-added keys, sections and `[[…]]` tables — is preserved byte-for-byte. A
  same-answers re-run is byte-identical.
  [verified: `ClusterInitCommandRerunTest.rerun_sameAnswers_isByteIdentical_keepingEveryCommentAndSectionInOrder`
  (three re-runs, 35 comment lines, section order) and
  `rerun_newAnswers_appendMissingSectionInPlace_keepingHandAddedSection` (insert-only diff,
  `[source.primary.worker]` lands after `[source.primary.core]`)]
- **Every edit needs consent — a differing value AND a missing key, section or rule.** The plan is
  listed first (`section.key: <old> → <new>`, `+ section.key`, `+ …allow_ingress[port=…, …]`); batch
  mode refuses (`OutputDiffers`, non-zero, file untouched) unless the new `--merge` flag consents,
  interactive mode asks once with default untouched. An appended `[[allow_ingress]]` rule is not
  harmless: one the operator narrowed from `0.0.0.0/0` or deleted is, to the merge, a missing
  generated rule, and appending it re-opens the port (verify-1087 r2 B4). Only an empty plan is
  consent-free, and it writes nothing (`Unchanged <path>`, mtime and mode untouched).
  [verified: `rerun_batch_refusesToRevertAHandTunedValue_namingOldAndNew`,
  `rerun_batch_withMerge_appliesTheNewAnswer_andRewritesOnlyThatLine` (one-line `diff`, the
  operator's comment survives), `rerun_interactive_defaultKeepsTheHandTunedValue`,
  `rerun_interactive_yesAppliesTheNewAnswer`,
  `rerun_withMerge_appliesAChangeAndAnAdditionTogether_eachAtItsOwnLine` (a rewrite and an
  insertion in one run, each on its own line),
  `rerun_cloud_refusesToReopenANarrowedIngressRule_withoutMerge_andNamesItByCidr` (an 8070 rule
  narrowed to `198.51.100.0/24`: batch refused naming `+ …[port=8070, …, source_cidr="0.0.0.0/0"]`,
  file byte-identical; with `--merge` appended and reported by CIDR),
  `rerun_newAnswers_appendMissingSectionInPlace_keepingHandAddedSection` (a missing section is
  refused without `--merge` too), `rerun_interactive_listsAdditions_andEnterLeavesTheFileUntouched`,
  `rerun_unchanged_doesNotRewriteTheFile`; mutation: ignoring consent so the existing value
  always wins reddens the three "applies" tests]
- **An operator-added `[[source.primary.firewall.allow_ingress]]` rule survives a cloud re-run and is
  listed as kept.** Generated elements are matched by their scalar keys but `description`; missing
  ones are appended after the file's last element; nothing is removed, so a changed `--admin-cidr`
  adds the new admin rules and keeps the old ones listed.
  [verified: `rerun_cloud_keepsAnOperatorAddedIngressRule_andListsIt` — file byte-identical, rule
  count +1, the kept listing names port 9100]
- **The report line is true in both directions**: `Merged into <path>: updated N key(s) — …; added N
  key(s) — …; kept N key(s) init does not generate — …` names every rewritten, appended and kept key,
  table-array elements included, or says `already matches the answers, nothing changed`.
  [verified: `rerun_newAnswers_appendMissingSectionInPlace_keepingHandAddedSection` (kept and added
  keys named), `InPlaceTomlMergeTest` (kept lists `rules[port=1]`)]
- **The interactive wizard and the merge question share one stdin reader** (`ClusterInitCommand.prompt`,
  passed to `ClusterConfigWizard`). Each used to wrap `System.in` in its own buffered reader, so on a
  piped stdin the wizard's reader drained the input and the merge question always read EOF and took
  its default. [verified: `rerun_interactive_yesAppliesTheNewAnswer` drives both through one
  `System.in`; mutation: a fresh `Prompt` at the question reddens it]
- **A file the merge cannot read is refused (`OutputUnreadable`, naming the reason, the file and
  `--force`), never clobbered** — including valid TOML on a feature the reader does not support, which
  the message now attributes to the reader rather than calling the file unparseable. A merged text
  that would not parse is refused the same way (`MergeError`) before anything is written.
  [verified: `rerun_refusesAnUnparseableExistingFile_ratherThanClobberingIt`,
  `rerun_refusesADuplicateKey_namingTheLine`,
  `rerun_refusesAFeatureTheMergeCannotRead_namingTheReason`]
- Assumes #1037 (#1019): the topology is given per tier (`--core-nodes` / `--worker-nodes`); the
  re-run pins add a worker tier with `--worker-nodes 2` against a core-only file.
- The line index mirrors `TomlParser`'s line rules (multi-line `"""`/`'''`/`[` values, quoted and
  dotted keys, `[[…]]` sub-tables) so a rewrite lands on the right line past them. A section the
  file holds only through dotted keys (`[cluster]` carrying `core.min = 3`) gets a header with ONLY
  its missing keys after the block holding them — it used to get init's whole block and be refused
  as a duplicate key (verify-1087 r2 S1). Inserted lines take the file's line ending (CRLF files
  stay CRLF). [verified: `InPlaceTomlMergeTest`, five cases incl.
  `dottedKeySection_getsAHeaderWithOnlyTheMissingKeys_afterTheBlockHoldingThem`;
  `rerun_crlfFile_getsCrlfInsertedLines`]
- Limits, stated: a multi-line value that is rewritten (with consent) collapses to init's single
  line, losing its trailing comment; `# Topology: …` header comments are comments and are not
  rewritten; a UTF-8 BOM is refused by the reader (as it always was for `bootstrap`). Batch mode no
  longer exits non-zero merely because the file exists — it does so only when the merge would edit
  the file and `--merge` is absent. [design intent — unverified]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #281: artifact-repo keyed by GAV only, so a coordinate's pom collided with its jar; delete kept the version listed; `<latest>` was deploy order)
- **`ArtifactStore` keyed every file of a Maven coordinate under one GAV key**, and
  `MavenProtocolHandler` parsed the classifier and extension only to discard them. A standard
  `mvn deploy` PUTs the jar then the pom: the pom came back `already-present` and was dropped, and
  `GET ….pom` served the jar's bytes; a `-sources.jar` collided the same way. Every file is now its
  own entry: `ArtifactFile(artifact, classifier, extension)` is the store's unit, the `Artifact`-typed
  operations address the coordinate's PRIMARY file (`jar`, no classifier) so slice resolution keeps
  its signature, and the handler passes the parsed file through — including Maven 3's timestamped
  SNAPSHOT names (`lib-1.0.0-20260914.010203-1-sources.jar` under `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT/`), which the
  first round still read as unclassified (verify-1132 B1); the plain `lib-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT-sources.jar`
  name addresses the same entry.
  [verified: `aether/resource/services/artifact-repo/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/resource/artifact/MavenFileRoundTripTest.java`
  — jar then pom both `uploaded`, each GET serves its own bytes, a classified jar is distinct, a
  never-deployed sibling is 404 (red at `2005ea7d2`); `#timestampedSnapshotDeploy_keysEveryFileSeparately`
  — jar/pom/sources/javadoc of one timestamped deploy each under their own `<file>/meta`,
  `<versions>` lists `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` once (red at `70059cfb6`)]
- **Storage format (CTO ruling, session 19):** one metadata key per file,
  `artifacts/<group>/<artifact>/<version>/<[classifier.]extension>/meta` — `…/jar/meta`,
  `…/pom/meta`, `…/sources.jar/meta` — the primary included, no special case. The pre-#281
  `…/<version>/meta` key is **not read**: artifact-store contents are cluster DHT state with no
  pre-GA compatibility promise, and a dual-read path would otherwise stay forever. The versions
  list stays per coordinate (a pom deploy re-registers the same version, idempotently), and each
  version keeps the list of its deployed files at `…/<version>/files`.
  [verified: `ArtifactStoreTest.KeyShapeTests` pins the literal key strings (incl. the file list's
  content) and that the legacy key is not consulted — a renamed segment reddens it]
  Note `ArtifactStore.Metrics.artifactCount` (`artifact.count` on the metrics route) now counts
  FILES — a standard deploy adds four.
- **`delete` removed only the metadata key and left the version listed.** It now also drops the
  file from the version's file list and, when that was the version's LAST file — primary or not —
  the version from the versions list (CTO ruling, round 2: a pom-only version is delisted with its
  pom; a version keeps its listing while any file of it exists). The content chunks are still not
  released: `[known: chunks are content-addressed and shared across artifacts and the
  cluster-shared DHT tier — a re-deploy of unchanged bytes under a new version shares every chunk,
  so releasing them safely needs a cluster-wide reference index; filed separately by the CTO]`.
  Note `ArtifactStore.delete` has no production caller today (`ARTIFACT_DELETE` is unserved, #1102).
  [verified: `ArtifactStoreTest.FileDeleteTests` — primary-with-pom-remaining and pom-with-jar-remaining
  keep the listing, the last file delists, a pom-only version delists with its pom, one of two
  versions survives, deleting a never-deployed file is a no-op]
- **`maven-metadata.xml` reported the LAST DEPLOYED version as `<latest>`.** `<latest>` is now the
  highest version and `<release>` the highest non-SNAPSHOT one, with `<versions>` ascending, by
  `VersionOrder`: numeric `major.minor.patch`, then the qualifier as Maven's `ComparableVersion`
  ranks it — `alpha` < `beta` < `milestone` < `rc`/`cr` < `snapshot` < none/`ga`/`final`/`release`
  < `sp` < any unknown qualifier (unknowns lexically among themselves); `a`/`b`/`m` alias only with
  a number (`a1`), bare they are unknown; equal tokens by their number; `<token>-SNAPSHOT` sorts
  directly below its `<token>` (`1.0.0-rc4-SNAPSHOT` < `1.0.0-rc4`). The first round placed
  unknowns below `snapshot` and a `<token>-SNAPSHOT` above its token and called that Maven's
  order (verify-1132 S1); every row is now checked against `ComparableVersion` 3.9. Still not the
  full algorithm: no dotted qualifier lists, no digit/letter splitting inside a token.
  [verified: `VersionOrderTest` (24 ordered pairs incl. `1.0.0-rc4` < `1.0.0`, `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` <
  `1.0.0`, `1.0.0` < `1.0.0-sp1` < `1.0.0-custom`, `alpha` < `beta` < `rc1`, `rc4-SNAPSHOT` < `rc4`),
  `MavenFileRoundTripTest#mavenMetadata_latestAndReleaseFollowVersionOrder_notDeployOrder`]
- `ArtifactStoreError` records now name the file (`org.example:lib:1.0.0:pom`), so a missing pom is
  reported as a missing pom. The operator doc's "Key Format" (`aether/docs/operators/artifact-repository.md`)
  now states the per-file keys and that chunks are content-addressed, not coordinate-keyed.
  `[known: #1102 — `PUT/GET …/1.0.0-SNAPSHOT/maven-metadata.xml` (version-level metadata, the last
  step of every SNAPSHOT deploy) still fails with 400: `parseMetadataPath` reads the dotted version as
  the artifactId; pre-existing, the #1102 positional-parse family]`
  [unverified: the versions-list get-then-put race (ticket item 4) is unchanged and now also covers
  removal and the file list; the hash helpers' swallowed exceptions and the checksum GET's
  404-for-500 (item 4) are untouched.]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #280: retry was idempotency-blind, logging leaked request/result content, metrics flags were ignored)
- **R26 — the retry interceptor retried every failure.** `RetryMethodInterceptor` handed each call to core `Retry`, which stops only on `Cause.Terminal`; a slice's own business verdict (`InsufficientFunds`) is unclassified and was re-driven as eagerly as a timeout, on methods that may not be idempotent. The interceptor cannot tell a business failure from an infrastructure one by origin, so retry is now **opt-in by classification**: core gains `Cause.Transient` (`isTransient()`, the mirror of `Cause.Terminal`; `Causes.transientCause(String)` beside `Causes.terminal`), `RetryConfig` gains `retry_on` — `TRANSIENT` (default: only a cause that declares itself transient is retried) or `NON_TERMINAL` (the behaviour before this change, for a method whose failures are all infrastructural but not yet classified) — and **core `Retry` gains `execute(operation, Predicate<Cause> retryable)` — a new abstract method on a public interface, source-compatible for every caller and source-incompatible for an external implementor of `Retry`, of which this repository has none — the policy evaluated on EVERY failure inside the loop**: a failure the policy refuses ends the call at once with that cause, on attempt one or attempt N alike, at DEBUG (neither the loop giving up nor a terminal verdict, which stay WARN). Every `Retry` line — the WARN on giving up or on a terminal cause, the DEBUG per attempt — now names the cause's TYPE, never its message: the message is where a business cause carries personal data, and the give-up WARN is the one line that reaches INFO (review of #1088, S9). [verified: `RetryLoggingBoundTest#giveUpLines_nameTheCauseType_neverItsMessage` — a cause carrying a card number: no line at any level contains it, the type is named; red with the message restored] The interceptor is `retry.execute(() -> method.apply(request), retryOn::retries)`; `max_attempts` counts calls at the method, the first included. (Round 1 applied the policy to the first failure only and then handed the budget to the plain loop, so a business verdict on attempt two was re-driven to the budget — review of #1088, B1.) [verified: `RetryInterceptorPredicateTest` (`aether/resource/interceptors`) — unclassified failure: 1 attempt under the default (was 3, red at the base), original cause returned; `Cause.Transient` failure: 3 attempts; `NON_TERMINAL` opt-in retries the unclassified failure; a budget of 1 makes no retry; transient-then-success returns the success; **transient-then-business stops at 2 calls and two-transient-then-business at 3 under a budget of 5**; a `Cause.Terminal` is never retried under either policy. `RetryTest#shouldStopWhenThePredicateRefusesALaterFailure` / `#shouldRetryWhileThePredicateAdmits` (`core`) pin the loop itself. Mutations: gating the predicate to the first failure reddens the two transient-then-business pins and the core pin; widening `TRANSIENT` to non-terminal reddens the unclassified pin] [verified: `RetryConfigTomlBindingTest#config_retryOn_bindsFromToml`, `#config_omittedRetryOn_fallsBackToTransient`]
- **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE.** A retry-intercepted method whose failure is an UNCLASSIFIED cause is no longer retried; only a `Cause.Transient` is. Existing `@Retry`-style declarations over unclassified causes stop retrying unless the section sets `retry_on = "NON_TERMINAL"` (explicit opt-in — retrying an unclassified failure is a decision, never a default, the #665 rule) or the cause is classified. When the policy declines a non-terminal cause it logs ONE DEBUG line through SLF4J (`org.pragmatica.aether.resource.interceptor.RetryMethodInterceptor`) naming the cause type and the policy — on whichever attempt it happens — so a retry that "stopped working" is findable without being a per-business-failure WARN. [verified: `RetryInterceptorPredicateTest` — default declines an unclassified cause (1 attempt), retries a `Cause.Transient` (3), `NON_TERMINAL` retries the unclassified (3), a `Cause.Terminal` is never retried under either policy (1 each); reverting the policy or the budget guard reddens the named pin] `RetryConfigTomlBindingTest`'s end-to-end fixture failed with a generic cause whose MESSAGE said "transient" and whose type said nothing; it now implements `Cause.Transient` — the fixture says what the prose always claimed.
- **Classification pass — every cause family a retry interceptor can see, and what the default now does with it.** The space: causes a slice method can return at CALL time — its resource clients' errors, invocation errors when it calls another slice, core utility errors, and its own business verdicts. Node-internal, CLI, Forge, provisioning-time and config-binding families (`SliceLoadingFailure`, `ResourceProvisioningError`, `ConfigError`, `TopicConfigError`, `EntityProvisioningError`, `DeploymentError`, `AbTestDeploymentError`, WAL/segment/replication internals…) never reach a slice method's result and are out of the space. Legend: **T** = now `Cause.Transient` (retried by default); **X** = `Cause.Terminal` (never retried); **U** = unclassified (retried only under `NON_TERMINAL`).
  - `core` `CoreError`: `Timeout` **T**; `Cancelled`, `Fault`, `Exception` **U**. `CircuitBreakerError.CircuitBreakerOpenError` **T** (carries `retryTime`). `RateLimiterError.LimitExceeded` **T**. `Causes.cause(...)` generic causes, parse errors, `FileError`, `StreamError` (io) **U**.
  - `slice-api`: `ResourceCapacityExhausted` — `isTransient()` now answers `transientCapacity()`, so every marker-bearing cause is **T** per instance (`StreamError.General` constants, `StreamError.ReshufflePaced`); `RateGuardError.LimitExceeded` **T**; `SliceRuntimeError`, `SliceBridge.BridgeError`, `StreamAccess`/`StreamPublisher`/`StreamRegistry`/`StreamVersionSpec`/`ResourceAddress`/`ResourceVersion` `General` enums **U**.
  - `resource-api` `DatabaseConnectorError`: `ConnectionFailed`, `TimedOut`, `PoolExhausted` **T**; `TransactionRolledBack` **T** (a serialization failure or deadlock rollback is the textbook retryable class, and the interceptor retries the whole method — the whole transaction — which is the right unit; round 1 left it U with a reason the type's own docs contradicted, review of #1088 S7); `QueryFailed`, `ConstraintViolation`, `TransactionNotActive`, `ResultNotFound`, `MultipleResults`, `ConfigurationError`, `DatabaseFailure` **U**. `RowDecodeError` **U**. `TransactionError` (aspect): all **U**. `HttpClientError` (`@Http` typed layer): `SerializationFailed`, `DeserializationFailed`, `RequestFailed`, `RequestFailedWithBody` **U** — the status is available, an HTTP-aware retry policy is the R7/#270 feature, not this change (note: it leaves a 503/429 from an `@Http` call, the commonest transient a slice sees, unretried by default until then). PR #1080 adds a terminal `InvalidRequest` to this family on its own branch; not cited here because it is not at this head.
  - `integrations/net/http-client` `HttpClientError`: `ConnectionFailed`, `Timeout` **T**; `RequestFailed`, `InvalidResponse`, `Failure` **U**.
  - `integrations/net/smtp` `SmtpError` and `integrations/email-http` `HttpEmailError`: classified in **PR #1075** (stacked on this one): SMTP `ConnectionFailed`, `Timeout`, any 4yz reply **T**; 5yz replies, and auth/TLS/protocol refusals with a 5yz code **X**; HTTP-email `RequestFailed` 5xx/408/429 **T**, other 4xx and `AuthError`/`VendorNotFound` **X**. Not marked here to keep one file with one owner.
  - DB drivers: `JdbcError`/`JooqError`/`R2dbcError` `ConnectionFailed`, `Timeout` **T**; `JdbcError.TransactionRollback`, `JooqError.TransactionRollback` **T** ("deadlock, serialization failure"); `JpaError.PessimisticLock`, `QueryTimeout`, `OptimisticLock` **T** ("modified by another transaction" — retry the transaction); postgres-async `SqlError.ChannelClosed`, `PoolExhausted`, `CommunicationError` **T**, and the `ServerError` subtypes for SQLSTATE class 40 (`ServerErrorTransactionRollback`: `40001 serialization_failure`, `40P01 deadlock_detected`) and class 53 (`ServerErrorInsufficientResources`) **T** as classes; classes 08 and 57 **per SQLSTATE**, because a class-wide mark would admit the one state that must never be retried — `08007 transaction_resolution_unknown`, a COMMIT whose reply was lost, where a retry re-runs a possibly committed write, the very R26 hazard (review of #1088, S8): `ServerConnectionException` is **T** for `08001`, `08004`, `08006` and **U** for `08007`, `08P01`; `ServerErrorOperatorIntervention` is **T** for `57P01 admin_shutdown`, `57P02 crash_shutdown`, `57P03 cannot_connect_now` and **U** for `57P04 database_dropped` and `57014 query_canceled` — ruled NOT transient: a statement_timeout cancel should surface, not be re-driven; every other member (constraint violations, query failures, `NoResult`/`MultipleResults`, `TransactionRequired`, `EntityNotFound`, `ConnectionPoolClosed`, configuration, the data/syntax/grantor `ServerError` subtypes, `DatabaseFailure`) **U**. `R2dbcError` has no rollback member.
  - `integrations/dht` `DHTError`: `PeerUnreachable`, `QuorumNotReached`, `NoAvailableNodes`, `OperationTimeout`, `MigrationInProgress` **T**; `StaleEpochWrite` **U**.
  - `aether-stream`, the publish/read path a slice reaches through `StreamPublisher.publish()` / `StreamAccess`: `StreamError.StreamConfigNotYetVisible`, `OwnerCatchupPending`, `LinearizableRoundTimeout`, `ReshufflePaced` **T**; `StreamForwardError.RemotePublishRetryable` **T** (the forwarder's own retryable marker), and `StreamForwardError.General.FORWARD_TIMEOUT`, `READ_FORWARD_TIMEOUT`, `GOVERNOR_UNAVAILABLE`, `STREAM_FORWARD_UNAVAILABLE` **T** (a forward timeout is a timeout; a governor not yet elected passes) with `READ_RESPONSE_OVERSIZED` **U**; `ReplicationError.General.REPLICATION_TIMEOUT`, `NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS` **T** (replica availability gates the publish ack when `min_sync_replicas > 1` — the same passing condition as `DHTError.QuorumNotReached`; round 1 wrongly scoped these out as "replication internals", review of #1088 S6); `EventTooLarge`, `CursorExpired`, `SeedRejected`, `StreamNotFound`, `PartitionOutOfRange`, `EventProcessingFailed`, `PartitionCeilingExceeded`, `PartitionCapExceeded`, `StaleEpochAppend`, `NotCurrentOwner`, `StaleEpochRead`, `RemotePublishFailed`, `ReadForwardFailed`, `PgStreamError` **U**.
  - `aether-invoke` `SliceInvokerError`: `NoEndpointsError`, `TimeoutError` **T**; `AllInstancesFailedError`, `InvocationError` (wraps the callee's cause — the callee's classification is what matters, and `Cause.Wrapped` is not unwrapped here), `MethodHandleError`, `SerializationError`, `RemoteInvocationError` **U**.
  - `durable-entity`: `EntityError.OwnershipNotYetCommitted`, `LinearizableUnavailable` **T**; `EntityLogError.FoldInProgress` **T**; every other `EntityError`/`EntityLogError` member and `EntityOwnerForward.ForwardRefused` **U**.
  - `notification` `NotificationError` (`BackendNotConfigured`, `UnsupportedChannel`, `DeliveryFailed`) **U** — `DeliveryFailed` already exhausted the sender's own classified retry (PR #1075); retrying it from the interceptor would double the schedule.
  - `storage` `StorageError`/`ContentStoreError`, codec errors (`JsonError`, `CodecError`, `WireFormatError`) **U**.
  - Slice-author causes: **U** by definition — the reason the default is opt-in.
  - **Reconciled against the reviewer's 473-type table (`verify-1088-cause-classification-2026-09-14.md`).** Adopted: the publish-path and rollback rows above. Kept, with the choice stated: `StreamError.General.BUFFER_FULL` stays **U** through `transientCapacity()` — it is STRONG-consistency backpressure that the writer, not a retry, relieves; the ownership/epoch races (`EntityError.NotCurrentOwner`/`StaleOwnerEpoch`/`StaleEpochRead`, `EntityLogError.ReplicationBarrierUnmet`/`PartitionNotHeld`, `StreamError.NotCurrentOwner`/`StaleEpochRead`) stay **U** because they are transient only if the retry re-enters routing, which is true of the outermost interceptor and false of an inner one — the author knows which; `StorageError.TierFull`/`TierNotAdmitted` and `ResolverError.RequestTimeout` stay **U** (not on a slice's call path today); `SliceInvokerError.AllInstancesFailedError` stays **U** (every instance failed at that moment — often the same verdict N times). Nothing the table calls terminal is marked transient here, and nothing marked transient here does the table call terminal.
  - **Two boundaries erase the classification and are NOT fixed here, named so nobody expects the marks to cross them:** a remote slice's cause crosses the invoke wire as text (`SliceInvokerError.RemoteInvocationError`, `DeserializedCause`), and `Cause.Wrapped` does not delegate `isTransient()`/`isTerminal()` to its `origin()`. A retry interceptor on the CALLING slice therefore sees the callee's transient failure as unclassified. The invoke-wire loss is #275; the `Cause.Wrapped` non-delegation has no ticket yet (ticket draft in the report).
  [verified: `TransientClassificationTest` in `aether/resource/interceptors` (core, slice-api, resource-api, http-client, dht rows) and in `integrations/db/{jdbc,jooq,r2dbc,jpa,postgres-async}`, `aether/aether-stream`, `aether/aether-invoke`, `aether/resource/durable-entity` — each asserts its **T** members are transient and not terminal, and a sample of **U** members stays unclassified; removing `Cause.Transient` from `DHTError` reddens the interceptors pin. `postgres-async`'s tests are skipped by default (`postgres-async.skipTests=true`); its pin ran with `-Dpostgres-async.skipTests=false`]
- `jbct-lint`'s `CauseHierarchies` recognises `Cause.Transient` as a mixin alongside `Terminal`/`Wrapped`, so a record `implements X, Cause.Transient` is a cause variant to the linter. [verified: `CausePackNearMissTest#qualifiedTransientMixin_marksVariant` — a value-discarding record implementing only `Cause.Transient` draws `JBCT-CAUSE-01`; with the widening reverted it is invisible to the pack and the test reddens]
- **R28 — logging.** `LogConfig.logConfig(name[, level])` defaulted `logArgs`/`logResult` to `true`, logging every request's and result's `toString()` unredacted; both now default to `false` (the TOML binder treats every field as mandatory, so this reaches programmatic callers). Every injection point logged through one logger named `LoggingMethodInterceptor`; each now logs through `LoggerFactory.getLogger(config.name())`, so one method's level is tunable. [verified: `LoggingInterceptorPrivacyTest` — defaults, and the logger's name equals the configured name (read reflectively, red at the base with the class name); reverting `LogConfig` reddens the two default pins, reverting the interceptor reddens the logger pin]
- **R28 — request-id correlation.** Round 1 said "lines carry no request-id"; that was false for the entry line and half-false for the exit line (review of #1088, S2): `InvocationContext` puts `requestId` in the SLF4J MDC around the slice call and the entry line carried it, but the exit line lost it whenever the promise resolved on another thread — the normal case. The interceptor now captures the MDC at entry and re-applies it around the exit line (restoring the logging thread's own afterwards), with no new dependency. Under the privacy defaults the exit line also names the OUTCOME — `ok` / `failed <CauseType>`, the type only, never the message (S3), so a failure is distinguishable from a success again. `resource-reference.md` corrected. [verified: `LoggingInterceptorExitLineTest` — a recording SLF4J logger pairing each line with the MDC its logging thread saw: the exit line of a promise resolved on another thread after the callback is registered carries the entry's `rid-42` (red with the carry removed); the exit line of a failing call reads `failed Declined` and never contains the cause's message; a success reads `ok` without the value. Mutation: removing the outcome reddens the two outcome pins]
- **R28 — `MetricsConfig.recordTiming` / `recordCounts` were bound and ignored** (a timer always, a counter never). `record_timing` now selects the timer `<name>.<outcome>` and `record_counts` a counter `<name>.<outcome>.count` — a separate meter name because Micrometer refuses two meter types under one id. [verified: `MetricsInterceptorFlagsTest` — timing off records no timer; counts on records a counter of 1; timing on / counts off records only the timer; reverting the interceptor reddens the first two]
- **R27 — NOT in this change and stated as left:** circuit-breaker and rate-limit metrics are a feature (owner: "Deferred post-GA: retry metrics"); the per-node scope of the rate limiter is already documented in the RateGuard section.
- `resource-reference.md`: `retry_on` row and example; `max_attempts` says "the first included"; `log_args`/`log_result` rows say the content is unredacted and personal until proven otherwise; `record_counts` names its meter.
- **What is NOT verified.** [unverified: any deployed slice's behaviour under the new default — no bundled slice declares a retry interceptor with a classified cause; the change is pinned at the interceptor.]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #279: the cache interceptor failed closed, `max_entries` capped nothing, and a shared section captured one method's `@Key` for every method)
- **(1) Fail-closed.** `CacheMethodInterceptor.cacheAside` chained `cache.get(key).flatMap(…)` and `writeThrough` chained `cache.put(…)`, so a backend failure — a DHT outage — failed the business call: a cache outage was a service outage. A backend `get` failure now reads as a **miss** (the method runs, its value is returned) and a `put` failure is absorbed (the completed write's result stands), for every strategy — `cacheAside` and `writeBack` puts go through the same `store` as `writeThrough` and are logged the same way. After a failed put a best-effort `remove(key)` follows, also absorbed, so a value-specific refusal does not leave the pre-write value to be served (a full outage fails the remove too). All logged at DEBUG through SLF4J, deliberately: a per-call WARN during an outage would be an unbounded log on the hottest path (#718's measured lesson). `WRITE_AROUND` was already fire-and-forget. **The fail-open covers a backend failure that arrives as a failed promise AND the DHT backend's codec throws**: `DHTCacheBackend` lifts `decode`/`encode` into `Result`s, because `SliceCodec.read` throws on an unknown type tag (a stale entry written by a codec that no longer knows its type — and distributed entries never expire, item 3) and `write` on an unregistered class, and a throw inside a promise mapper is neither a miss nor a failure: with the real client the slice call hung, the method never ran. Lifted, a stale-codec entry is a miss and an unencodable value a dropped put. [verified: `CacheFailOpenTest` (`aether/resource/interceptors`) — `cacheAside`/`readThrough` with a backend whose `get` fails: method called once, value returned, backend consulted once; `writeThrough` with a failing `put`: value returned, put attempted; a put-refusing backend pre-seeded with `OLD`: `NEW` returned and `OLD` removed; control: a failing METHOD still fails. `DHTCacheBackendCodecFailureTest` — the real `DHTCacheBackend` over a fake `DHTClient` and a codec that throws: `cacheAside` on a stale entry runs the method once and returns its value, `writeThrough` on an unencodable value returns the method's value, and the backend's own `get`/`put` are failed promises, not throws. Red at the base with `must be fail-open, got get: backend down`; reverting the interceptor reddens the 3 fail-open pins, removing the invalidation reddens the stale-entry pin, reverting the DHT lift reddens the 3 codec pins with `IllegalArgument Unknown type tag 4242` / `No codec registered` escaping raw]
- **(4) Unbounded `InMemoryCache`.** `put` evicted only EXPIRED entries when full and then inserted regardless, so `max_entries` bounded nothing for a hot cache. The store is now an access-ordered `LinkedHashMap` evicting its least-recently-used entry on overflow (expired entries go first), guarded by the instance monitor. [verified: `InMemoryCacheTest$Bound` — 10 puts into a cap of 3 with nothing expired leave ≤ 3 present (was 10); the touched entry survives and the untouched one is the victim; an overwrite at the bound evicts nothing. Reverting `InMemoryCache` reddens the first two. The monitor is pinned deterministically by `InMemoryCacheTest$ConcurrentAccess#mixedOperations_underContention_neverThrow_andHonourTheCap` — 16 threads × 20,000 get/put/remove over 200 keys into a cap of 64: no exception and ≤ 64 present; with the `synchronized` blocks removed it reddens every run (`ConcurrentModificationException` from the access-ordered map), where the pre-existing 8-thread no-data-loss test reddened only 2 runs in 3]
- **(2) Shared-section `@Key` capture.** The generator deduplicated interceptor provisions by `(type, config)` and `findKeyInfoForInterceptor` returned the FIRST matching method's extractor, so two `@Key` methods under one config section shared one instance keyed by the first method's request type — a `ClassCastException` on the second method's first call, or a wrong key when the types coincided. A key-bearing method now gets its own provision (`provisionKey` = `(type, config)` + method name), carrying its own extractor; key-less methods keep sharing one instance per section, because sharing is the point for rate limits and circuit breakers. What is shared underneath — the named cache or idempotency store — is shared by the factory's `SharedByName` registry (#894), not by the generated variable, so per-method instances do not duplicate caches. [verified: `SliceProcessorTest#should_provision_a_key_bearing_interceptor_per_method_when_the_config_section_is_shared` (`jbct/slice-processor`) — two `@Key` methods under `cache.shared` generate two `provide(MethodInterceptor.class, "cache.shared", …)` calls with `GetUserRequest::userId` AND `GetOrderRequest::orderId`; red at the base (second extractor absent); reverting the generator reddens it]. No envelope bump: `ENVELOPE_FORMAT_VERSION` is frozen at 1000 until GA (owner ruling on #386). [mechanism: root `mvn clean install -DskipTests` compiles every regenerated factory in the tree — see the report for the reactor result]
- **(3) DHT TTL and cross-node invalidation — NOT fixed here, stated.** `DHTClient` has no expiry primitive (`put(byte[], byte[])` only; repo grep for ttl/expire in `integrations/dht`: none), so honouring `ttl_seconds` on `DISTRIBUTED` is a DHT feature, not an interceptor fix; cross-node invalidation for `TIERED` is owner-deferred post-GA (ticket comment 2026-08-26). The doc's `TIERED` row already carried the gap; the `ttl_seconds` and `max_entries` rows now say which store each governs, and the `DISTRIBUTED` row states the fail-open behaviour. [design intent — unverified]
- **What is NOT verified.** [unverified: fail-open against a real DHT outage on a cluster — the pins use a fake `DHTClient`; the real client's failure shapes (timeouts vs. refusals) arrive as failed promises (`DHTError`, now `Cause.Transient` in #1088) and are covered by the same `recover` by reading, not by a live run.]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #276 R20: the legacy `ConfigService` facade threw on a malformed numeric value)
- **`NodeDeploymentManager.ConfigServiceConfigFacade` parsed `requireLong`/`requireDouble`/`getLong`/`getDouble` with `Long.parseLong` / `Double.parseDouble` inside `.map`**, so a config value that is not a number (`pool.size = "twelve"`) escaped as `NumberFormatException` out of a facade whose whole contract is `Result`/`Option`. `ConfigService` exposes no numeric getter beyond `getInt`, so the adapter must parse; it now parses through core's `Number.parseLong` / `Number.parseDouble` — the exception boundary — and maps a parse failure at the `Result` boundary to a cause that **names the key and the value** (`Config key pool.size is not a long: "twelve"`); `Number.parseX`'s own cause is a `Causes.fromThrowable` whose message is the stack trace with the key nowhere in it, and on the live path that landed verbatim in the generated slice's `configLog.warn` (review of #1092, SF-2). On `requireLong`/`requireDouble` a malformed value is therefore a named failure distinct from the absent-key failure (`requireInt` routes through `ConfigService.getInt`, which folds a malformed value into absent — pre-existing, outside R20, unchanged). On the `Option`-returning `get*` it reads as absent — the same behaviour `ConfigurationProvider`'s own `getLong`/`getDouble` give the slice-api `ConfigProviderFacade`, and a conflation of malformed with absent that is tracked under #1098, not changed here. This facade is what `NodeDeploymentState.buildConfigFacade` hands a slice when its per-slice config service is absent. [verified: `ConfigServiceConfigFacadeNumericTest` (`aether/aether-deployment`) — four pins asserting no throw and a failed `Result` / empty `Option` for `"twelve"` and `"half"`; the two `require*` pins also assert the message names the value AND the key and has no newline; red at the base with `NumberFormatException: For input string: "twelve"`. Mutations: reverting `NodeDeploymentManager` reddens exactly the four pins; folding `requireDouble`'s malformed value into `MISSING_KEY` reddens its pin (round 1 had left that reader unpinned); dropping the named-cause mapping reddens `requireLong`'s pin on the missing key]
- **R21 — RateGuard is node-local: documented scope, not a defect, and left** — by the CTO's scope ruling for #276, not by the doc alone: `resource-reference.md`'s RateGuard section states `Scope today: Local (type="local"); distributed is #144` but not "cluster rate = limit × instances", and `type` is neither implemented nor removed. Two of the ticket's R21 sub-claims are stale at this tip: `DefaultRateGuard` DOES honour `burst` (`RateLimiter.builder().burst(config.burst())`), and `remaining = 0` on the `LimitExceeded` path is the true value at the moment a token-bucket refusal is issued. `requireStringList` remains refused by name in the legacy adapter (`ConfigProviderFacade` implements it for the slice path); not in this ticket's acceptance and not changed.
- **What is NOT verified.** [unverified: dependents' test suites (`aether/node`, `aether/aether-control`) — the change is confined to four method bodies with no signature change; the module's own 1,021 tests are green.]

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #275: slice-to-slice routing had no liveness filter, so a call to a dead node hung for the invoker timeout)
- **Slice-to-slice endpoint selection never consulted membership.** `SliceInvokerImpl` picked from `EndpointRegistry`, a projection of committed `NodeArtifactKey` rows that outlive a dead node until the cluster deployment manager's removal cleanup lands, so a new invocation was round-robined (or affinity-pinned, or failed over) onto a node membership already knew was gone and waited out the 20s `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. The HTTP forward path had `AccessibilityFilter` (`MembershipFsm.reachableMembers`: every member not co-confirmed DEAD) since the H7 fix; the facade path had nothing. [mechanism: `SliceInvokerImpl.selectEndpoint` / `selectEndpointWithAffinity` / `selectEndpointWithFailover` at `2005ea7d2` read the registry only; `handleNodeDeparture` retries only in-flight invocations, after `NodeRemoved`]
- `SliceInvoker.setAccessibilityFilter(AccessibilityFilter)` (default no-op on the interface, overridden by the production invoker) is wired in `AetherNode` to the same filter the forwarder uses. Every selection path now skips a registered endpoint whose node the filter rejects: plain selection becomes the excluding round-robin, an affinity target that is inaccessible yields to that filtered selection, and failover excludes inaccessible nodes together with the ones that already failed. Computed per call from the registry's current rows, so a node's return is seen on the next call. [verified: `SliceInvokerLivenessFilterTest` — four cases (request/response, fire-and-forget, affinity, failover) red without the filtering logic, green with it; removing only the affinity filter reddens exactly the affinity case, removing only the failover exclusion reddens exactly the failover case]
- **The exclusion is scoped to the candidate set each arm actually draws from — the weighted-routing pick spans every version of the base, so a version-scoped exclusion could not narrow it.** During an active deployment both the plain and the failover arm hand selection to `EndpointRegistry.selectEndpointWithRouting`, which builds its candidates from `findEndpointsForBase` — all versions — and splits them old/new. The exclusion was computed from `findEndpoints(slice, …)`, the invoked version only, so a co-confirmed-DEAD node hosting only the OTHER version was named by nothing, the "anything excluded?" fast path saw an empty set, and the weighted pick handed out the dead node. That is the ticket's hang, on exactly the path a rolling deployment exercises. `selectEndpointWithRouting` now takes the excluded set and drops those endpoints **before** the old/new split, and the invoker computes it over `findEndpointsForBase` for both routed arms. [mechanism: `SliceInvoker.inaccessibleNodesForBase` / `excludedNodesForBase` feed the new `EndpointRegistry.selectEndpointWithRouting(…, Set<NodeId> excludeNodes)`; the 5-arg overload remains as a default delegating with an empty set] [verified: `SliceInvokerRoutingLivenessFilterTest` — reverting both production files to the pre-fix head reddens 5 of its 7 cases; neutering only the registry's candidate filter reddens 6; handing only the plain arm an empty exclusion reddens 4 and handing only the failover arm a version-scoped one reddens exactly `weightedRouting_failoverFirstAttempt_neverSelectsDeadNodeHostingOnlyTheOtherVersion` — disjoint red sets, so the two call sites are pinned independently. No mutation reddens `SliceInvokerLivenessFilterTest`, so this hunk is independent of the single-version arms]
- **Excluding a dead node no longer costs the deployment its weighted split.** The old code bypassed the weighted pick entirely once anything was excluded, falling back to a round-robin over the invoked version — so a single dead node anywhere in the base silently served 100% of traffic from one version while the deployment believed a canary was running. Now the routed arms stay routed and simply carry the exclusion. [verified: `SliceInvokerRoutingLivenessFilterTest.weightedRouting_stillSplitsAcrossVersions_whenAnUnrelatedNodeIsDead` — both live versions are still selected with a third node dead]
- **All candidates filtered out is an absence of endpoints, not an instance failure.** On the retry path a first selection that comes back empty reached `handleAllEndpointsFailed`, which published an `AllInstancesFailed` event with an empty attempt list and no cause, and failed the call with the untyped `AllInstancesFailedError("0 nodes attempted")` — telling an operator the instances failed for a call that never left the node, with a non-transient cause for a situation a replacement node resolves. It now fails with the transient `SliceInvokerError.NoEndpointsError` and publishes no event. [verified: `SliceInvokerRoutingLivenessFilterTest.weightedRouting_everyHostInaccessible_retryReportsNoEndpointsAndPublishesNoFailureEvent` — neutering the guard reddens it] [verified: `SliceInvokerRoutingLivenessFilterTest.weightedRouting_everyHostInaccessible_failsWithoutSending` — the plain path fails with zero sends, no fallback onto the filtered-out node]
- `[known: the filter cannot beat detection latency]` — a silently dead node is still selectable until SWIM co-confirms it DEAD, exactly as on the HTTP forward path; what closes is the window between DEAD and the KV row cleanup, and the affinity/failover/routed arms that previously ignored liveness altogether. `[unverified: end-to-end on a multi-node kill — pinned at the invoker's transport boundary only]`
- The deliberate reading of "reachable": NOT co-confirmed DEAD. A DEPARTING drainer and a SUSPECT member are still selectable — they are up and serving in-flight work, and the caller carries its own timeout — so only terminal DEAD drops out of selection. [verified: `MembershipFsmTest.ReachableMembersForEndpointSelection` (`departingMember_isStillReachable`, `suspectMember_isStillReachable`, `deadMember_isNotReachable`), alongside the pre-existing `ReachableMembers.reachableMembers_includesObservedAndDeparting_excludesOnlyDead`; narrowing `reachableMembers` to the DHT-routable set (which excludes DEPARTING) reddens exactly the two DEPARTING cases]
- **The production wiring is now pinned by a tripwire, because nothing else could see it.** `SliceInvoker.setAccessibilityFilter` is a `default` no-op on the interface and the invoker's field defaults to `AccessibilityFilter.IDENTITY`, so a wired invoker and an unwired one are identical until a node actually dies — deleting the single call site in `AetherNode` leaves **all 1449 `aether/node` tests green**, and the invoker-level pins cannot see it either because they set the filter on their own fixture. `InvokerAccessibilityFilterWiringTest` asserts the call edge exists, using the same bytecode reachability scanner `AlertingWiringLivenessTest` uses for #957. [verified: deleting `sliceInvoker.setAccessibilityFilter(accessibilityFilter)` from `AetherNode` and recompiling `aether/node` reddens it; restoring returns it to green — green/red/green, not reasoning]
- `[unverified: what the wiring test cannot assert]` — the scanner sees call edges, not arguments, so nothing pins that the filter handed to the invoker is the SAME instance the HTTP forward path consults, nor that its body is correct. A node-level behavioural pin would need a boot test; that remains open, and the forwarder's own filter argument has the identical hole, which predates this change.
- Not changed (findings 2 and 3 of #275, both API/wire design): remote failures still collapse to `RemoteInvocationError(String)` — a typed cause across `InvokeResponse` is a wire-format change; timeout/retry are still not caller-configurable on `SliceInvokerFacade` — a public API change. Both left for a ruling. `[design intent — unverified]` The plain `invoke` path's "no endpoint" outcome is still the untyped `NO_ENDPOINT_FOUND` rather than `NoEndpointsError`; that belongs to finding 2's cause taxonomy.

### Changed (2026-09-14 — #273 item 3: the cron clock source is documented as node-local)
- `@Scheduled` cron next-fire times come from the node's own wall clock (`Instant.now()`, UTC via `CronExpression`);
  no cluster clock, HLC not consulted. Stated in `ScheduledTaskManager.TaskOps.nextCronFireAt`'s javadoc and in
  `resource-reference.md` ("Clock Source"): ALL-mode fires per node at that node's reading of the boundary, SINGLE-mode
  uses the leader's clock and a leader change moves the reference, a stepping clock can double-fire or skip a boundary
  on that node. No behaviour change [mechanism: `nextCronFireAt` → `cron.delayUntilNext(Instant.now())`].

### Fixed (2026-09-14 — #272: @Scheduled cluster lifecycle — SINGLE-mode fires failed when the leader did not host the slice; ALL-mode fired on non-hosting nodes; also #273 item 1, ALL-mode eligibility on a draining node)
- **R12 (SINGLE): a leader that did not host the slice failed every fire with `SENDER_BRIDGE_NOT_FOUND` and wrote a failure state every interval, while the hosting node never saw a call.** The automatic fire is `SliceInvoker.invoke(artifact, method, Unit.unit())`; for a remote endpoint `sendFireAndForget` resolved the request's codec through a LOCAL slice bridge, which a non-hosting leader has none of. The `Unit` request needs no bridge: its wire form is fixed — the single VLQ byte `TAG_UNIT` (0) with an empty body, registered by `FrameworkCodecs.unitCodec` in the node codec that every slice codec layers over (`SliceStore` → `slice.codec(nodeCodec)` → `SliceCodec.sliceCodec(parent, …)`), so the callee's `DefaultSliceBridge.invoke` → `codec.decode(input)` → `CodecHolder.read` → `lookupByTag(0)` reads it back as `Unit` for a zero-argument method. The invoker now encodes a `Unit` fire-and-forget request with the node serializer it already holds and sends it on the EXISTING `InvokeRequest` frame; every other request type still requires a sender bridge. No new frame, tag or codec. [mechanism: `SliceInvokerImpl.encodeFireAndForgetRequest`; `SystemTags`/`FrameworkCodecs` `TAG_UNIT = 0`] [verified: `ScheduledSingleFireHostingTest` (Heavy, 3-node Ember, `test-full` `[scheduling.heartbeat]` SINGLE 10s, placement forced off the leader with a filler blueprint) — red at `2005ea7d2` with `hostHeartbeatCalls=0`, `consecutiveFailures=2`, `lastFailureMessage=No local SliceBridge available…` inside 20s; green after with `hostHeartbeatCalls=2`, `totalExecutions=2`, `consecutiveFailures=0`, the host's count read from its own `InvocationHandler` metrics; unit: `SliceInvokerUnitFireAndForgetTest` — the payload equals `{0x00}` and the framework codec decodes it to `Unit`, a non-`Unit` request still fails at the sender; removing the `Unit` branch reddens exactly it]
- **R12 (ALL) and #273 item 1: ALL-mode ran on every Following/Leading node with no hosting or draining input, so a non-hosting node registered a timer and wrote a failure state every interval, and a draining node kept firing.** ALL-mode eligibility is now `hosting ∧ ¬draining`, decided at timer registration (state entry and registry change) AND re-checked at every tick, so a slice unloaded on this node while another replica keeps the cluster-scoped key alive stops firing here without a state write. SINGLE-mode stays leader-owned and is NOT gated on hosting. `stateKeyFor` is unchanged: SINGLE writes the unscoped key from the one leader, ALL writes a per-node key — single writer per key as before. [mechanism: `ScheduledTaskManager.TaskOps.eligible` / `hostingAndNotDraining` / `shouldFire`] [verified: `ScheduledTaskManagerTest.allMode_nonHostingNode_registersNoTimerAndWritesNoState` (0 timers, 0 fires, 0 state writes over >=2 one-second intervals), `allMode_hostingLostAfterTimerStart_ticksAreSkippedSilently`, `singleMode_leaderNotHosting_stillStartsAndFires`; dropping the hosting term from `hostingAndNotDraining` reddens exactly the first two]
- **#273 item 1, round 2 — the drain gate had no producer and could never engage.** Round 1 keyed it on `MembershipDecision.NodeDraining(self)` / `NodeFailedDrain(self)` and routed both in `AetherNode`. Nothing in the product emits either: `MembershipDeltaProjector` is the exclusive emitter and emits only `nodeJoined` / `nodeRemoved`, and `MembershipDecision`'s own contract records that those four lifecycle variants "are no longer emitted — the synthetic per-node lifecycle-projection layer was removed in the membership-v2 finale". The code was present, its test was green, and the behaviour could not occur — the test constructed and dispatched the event itself, so it pinned its own fixture. On a real drain `ctx.draining` stayed `false` and the node kept firing for the whole grace window. The gate is now keyed on the drain edge that actually runs: `DrainProcedure.initiate` invokes its `drainInitiatedEmitter` once inside the `INACTIVE -> DRAINING` CAS, and `AetherNode.drainInitiatedEmitter` composes `ScheduledTaskManager.onDrainInitiated` into it — so all three triggers (QUORUM_LOSS, CORE_ABSENCE, COMMANDED) funnel through one hook. The two dead routes are removed. **The `NodeFailedDrain` restart arm is deleted rather than rewired: it has no producer AND no corresponding state.** `DrainProcedure` is `INACTIVE -> DRAINING -> EXITED` behind a single CAS with no transition back and no failure state, so a drained node halts and never returns to service; `ctx.draining` is therefore set once and never cleared. [mechanism: `DrainProcedure.initiate` -> `emitDrainInitiatedSafely` -> `AetherNode.drainInitiatedEmitter` -> `ScheduledTaskManager.onDrainInitiated` -> `TaskOps.cancelAllModeTimers`] [verified: `ScheduledTaskDrainWiringBootTest` (`aether/node`, DEFAULT reactor) boots a real node and delivers a real `ClusterSyncPing` whose `drainNodes` names it — the wire form the leader sends for an operator drain — then asserts the scheduler cancelled its ALL-mode timer; un-wiring the hook (`scheduledTaskDrainHookRef.set`) reddens exactly it, with `ConditionTimeout` on that assertion] [verified: `ScheduledTaskManagerTest.allMode_drainingSelf_stopsFiring` — removing `TaskOps.cancelAllModeTimers` from `onDrainInitiated` reddens it and `allMode_drainingSelf_doesNotReRegisterOnQuorumReEntryOrRegistryChange`, 2 of 31] [unverified: the leader-side half — HTTP route -> `DrainCommandRegistry` -> ping stamping — needs >=2 nodes and a management HTTP server, and is not exercised here]
- **The `¬draining` term itself is now pinned, and in round 1 it was not.** Round 1's changelog claimed "removing the drain edges reddens exactly the third"; measured, dropping `! ctx.draining.get()` from `hostingAndNotDraining` reddened nothing — the drain test asserted only the cancel, which `cancelAllModeTimers` performs on its own. That term is what stops a *re-registration* while draining, and `startEligibleTasks` runs again on every Following/Leading re-entry and on any schedule change, both of which outlive the start of a 30s grace window. `allMode_drainingSelf_doesNotReRegisterOnQuorumReEntryOrRegistryChange` drives a quorum loss and re-entry plus a new task after the drain and asserts 0 timers and no fire. [verified: dropping the `! ctx.draining.get()` term reddens exactly that one test, 1 of 31, on `[a Following re-entry must not re-register while draining]`] [verified: `allMode_notDraining_stillFiresAfterQuorumReEntry` is the opposite-direction control — a hosting, non-draining node re-registers and keeps firing after the same re-entry, so a predicate that excluded every node could not satisfy both]
- The pre-existing `allMode_startsOnNonLeaderNode` keeps its meaning with the stub invoker now modelling a HOSTING node by default (`hasLocalSlice` true unless told otherwise) — "every node" was always "every hosting node" in the runs that pinned it; the stub simply never said which.
- Status of the three findings, with the pinning tests: **R11** (schedule lost on scale-down) — already fixed at the tip: `NodeDeploymentState.doUnpublishScheduledTasks` removes the cluster-scoped key only when `artifactHostedElsewhere` is false, pinned by `NodeDeploymentStateScheduledTaskPauseTest.artifactHostedElsewhere_anotherLiveReplicaHostsTask_isTrue` / `_onlySelfHostsTask_isFalse` / `_otherReplicaUnloading_isFalse` — not re-fixed. **R12** — fixed here, above. **R13** (pause reset on republish) — already fixed at the tip: `buildValidatedScheduledTaskPutCommand` carries `existingPausedFlag(key)`, pinned by `existingPausedFlag_republishOverPausedValue_carriesPausedTrue` / `_republishOverRunningValue_carriesPausedFalse` / `_freshPublishWithNoExistingValue_defaultsFalse` and `withPaused_preservesScheduleFieldsAndSetsPausedTrue` — not re-fixed.
- Limits, tagged in the same namespace as the claims above so one `grep '\[unverified:'` returns them next to what they scope. **The headline SINGLE-mode claim's only end-to-end evidence does not run in CI:** `ScheduledSingleFireHostingTest` lives in `aether/forge/forge-tests`, which `aether/forge/pom.xml` puts behind the `with-e2e` profile, so it is absent from the default reactor and CI reports `heavy-forge-tests` as `skipped` `[unverified: the SINGLE-mode end-to-end fix is not covered by any default-reactor gate; its default-reactor evidence is the mechanism only — `SliceInvokerUnitFireAndForgetTest` (the `Unit` wire form) and `ScheduledTaskManagerTest.singleMode_leaderNotHosting_stillStartsAndFires` (leader-owned, not hosting-gated)]`. The ALL-mode negative and the drain gate are pinned in the manager's unit harness (one-second intervals, >=2 intervals observed) plus one real-node boot test `[unverified: ALL-mode on a real MULTI-NODE drain]`. A manual `/api/scheduled-tasks/inject` on a non-hosting node keeps the `hasLocalSlice` guard `ScheduledTaskRoutes` already had. A harness-only observation, not a product change: an Ember cluster started without a `ConfigurationProvider` builds no slice composite, so a slice's `[scheduling.*]` section from its jar is never resolved and no task is published — silently `[unverified: whether any production path can reach that silence]`.
- Two review NITs resolved by tracing rather than changing code, recorded because the reasoning is the result. **(a) An ALL-mode timer whose hosting ends is deliberately NOT cancelled**, only skipped per tick by `shouldFire`. Cancelling it would be cheaper and is wrong: re-registration depends on a registry change, and `ScheduledTaskRegistry.notifyIfChanged` notifies only when `scheduleChanged` — interval, cron, executionMode or paused — differs, so the identical-value republish a node issues when it re-loads the slice is SILENT. Cancelling would turn cheap timer churn into a task that stops for the process lifetime, which is worse than the churn and invisible to every test here [mechanism: `ScheduledTaskRegistry.notifyIfChanged` / `scheduleChanged`]. The same mechanism means a node that starts hosting AFTER state entry does not register its ALL-mode timer until the schedule changes — pre-existing, not introduced here, and filed separately. **(b) `shouldFire` is an entry check, so a drain beginning mid-invocation does not interrupt that invocation** — and the drain does not wait for it either: `InFlightRequestTracker.enter()` / `tryEnter()` have ZERO callers in `src/main` (positive control: the same search space and pattern shape finds `setAcceptingNewWork` at `DrainProcedure:190`), so the counter is always 0 and `onAllDrained` fires immediately. That is a defect in the drain's quiesce phase generally, not in scheduling, and is filed separately rather than widened into this PR `[unverified: whether any caller was intended to exist — established only that none does]`.

### Fixed (2026-09-13 — #1069: Heavy 5→7 scale probes sent the pre-#581 scale body and reported the HTTP 400 as a #336 stall)
- **`ScaleUpFiveToSevenProbeTest` and `ArtifactChurnSurvival5to7to5ProbeTest` still posted `{coreCount, expectedVersion}`** to
  `POST /api/v1/cluster/scale`. Since #581 the request is `ScaleRequest(source, role, count, expectedVersion)`, so the server
  refused every call with HTTP 400 `Type mismatch: expected int, got unknown`. Neither probe read the status: the rejected
  call left the configured count at 5, and the probes waited out their budget and reported a "5→7 stall … #336 reproducing
  IN-JVM". Every conclusion about #336/#467 drawn from them since #581 was measuring a refused HTTP call.
- Both probes now send `{source:"", role:"core", count, expectedVersion}` (the shape `PostRestartSlowRejoinDeficitFillProbeTest`, since deleted by #1533,
  already sent) and fail before any membership wait unless the response is 2xx, reports the requested `newCount`, and
  reports `configVersion` one past the fencing version it was sent. A transport failure also fails immediately.
- **`03-scaling/test-01-quorum-safety.sh` had the same stale body and passed without testing anything.** Its three rejection
  tests sent `{coreCount}` and accepted any `>= 400`, so the decoder's 400 satisfied them before the quorum or max check ran.
  They now send `{role, count, expectedVersion}` and require the refusal detail to name the validator's own message
  (`Quorum safety violation`, `Invalid core max`). The above-max case moves from 20 to 21, because 20 is even and the
  validator refuses it as `Invalid core count` before it compares against `coreMax`.
- `cluster-management-spec.md` documented a `{core_count, expected_version}` request and a 400 for quorum violations. It now
  shows the current request and response and the statuses the route actually returns (quorum violation is 409).
- **`EmberCluster.currentLeader()` answered from whichever node `ConcurrentHashMap` iterated first** (its leader view),
  and `status()` / `getLeaderManagementPort()` derive from it. After `addNode()` the first entry is the newborn, which
  holds no leader view, so every leader accessor said "no leader" while the elected leader was running; the two probes
  then counted membership on that newborn — which `MembershipFsm.seed` fills with the whole configured core set before a
  packet moves — and the ScaleUp probe declared 5→7 complete ~300 ms after `addNode()` while the leader still counted 5,
  and the churn probe's down-leg POST went to the newborn's management port and was refused 503 `No leader elected`.
  `currentLeader()` now names the running node whose own `isLeader()` holds
  `[verified: EmberClusterCurrentLeaderTest.currentLeader_isTheNodeClaimingLeadership_notTheFirstMapEntry — reverting to
  findFirst() reddens it with currentLeader()=None() while the leader is running]`.
- Both probes read the counted-core denominator from, and address the scale POST to, that leader only — no fallback to
  the first map entry — and a 7 is accepted only from a node that was a member at 5, so a count taken from a node the
  scale created fails the probe naming that node and what the leader counted at that instant
  `[verified: ScaleUpFiveToSevenProbeTest, ArtifactChurnSurvival5to7to5ProbeTest — with the first-entry read restored
  both fail "counted 7 cores on scale-7 … the node claiming leadership (scale-1) counts 5"; with that guard also removed
  the ScaleUp probe passes 279 ms after addNode() with leader=none, which is the pass the head shipped]`. With the leader
  read, 5→7 completes on the leader's FSM in 17.2–18.1 s in-JVM (n=2) and the churn's 7→5 down-leg is accepted (HTTP 200).
- **The churn probe's 7→5 leg was then accepted at the DEPARTING edge** (~0.5 s after the POST): `MembershipFsm` prunes a
  drainer from `coreCountedMembers()` the instant `drainNode` is requested, before its departure push has moved a chunk, and
  the count was read on the leader — itself a drain victim. A #427 regression would have stayed green. The down-leg is now
  accepted only at the terminal edge (both victims stopped and removed by `EmberCluster.handleSelfDrain`, a surviving leader
  counting exactly the survivor set, every victim `Dead` in its view, nothing `Departing`), with the survival read taken from
  that named survivor `[verified: with the terminal clauses removed the tripwire `requireTerminalOnSurvivor` fails at 511 ms —
  "accepted at the DEPARTING edge … churn-1 still sees departing=[churn-2, churn-1]"]`.
- **#1089 — the reconciler selects the LEADER as a drain victim and the DRAIN command can never reach it.**
  `LeaderReconciler.selectDrainVictims` does not exclude the leader (in Ember no id is ephemeral, the slice owners are
  excluded and the added nodes are inside the 30 s drain-safety grace, so the reversed-id mature seeds — the leader among
  them — are chosen first), and the command is delivered only on the leader's broadcast `ClusterSyncPing`, which
  `ClusterSyncState.dispatchPing` never sends to `self`. The leader never runs its `DrainProcedure`; it marks itself
  `Departing`, #1058 withdraws it to MEMBER when no acknowledgement arrives after the 15 s DEPARTING window, and it is
  selected again — until an added node passes the grace and is drained instead. Measured in-JVM at the merged head (n=3):
  `drainNode requested` for the leader **twice**, `DrainProcedure` for it **zero** times, **two** self-`Departing`→MEMBER
  withdrawals (~15 s each), the second victim (`churn-7`) requested only at ~+44 s, terminal edge at
  **49,972 / 50,853 / 51,213 ms** — a ~45 s detour against the ~5 s the non-leader victim needs. Before #1058 the leader
  wedged in DEPARTING and the edge was unreachable; in cloud the CTM's 60 s grace-terminate kills the leader ungracefully,
  no departure push — the #427 loss mode. No product change here (ruling C). `ArtifactChurnSurvival5to7to5ProbeTest` therefore carries an ENABLED tripwire,
  `leaderSelectedAsDrainVictim_neverDrains_tripwireUntil1089`, asserting that behaviour precisely (the leader listed ITSELF
  as `Departing` during the down-leg and is still a survivor at the terminal edge; its failure message says "#1089 landed —
  delete me") beside the enabled terminal-edge probe; both read one churn cycle
  `[verified: with the leader shielded from selection in the clone (shape B simulated, not the real fix) the tripwire
  reddens on "must have marked ITSELF Departing" while the probe stays green; at head both are green, down-leg terminal at
  50.0–51.2 s with victims churn-2 and churn-7 Dead and the leader intact]`. `ScaleUpFiveToSevenProbeTest` is unaffected
  and stays strict.

### Fixed (2026-09-13 — #1068: a rolled-back blueprint deploy could leave a slice instance that was re-deployed and served with no owning blueprint)
- **A rollback's UNLOAD is its own consensus round and can fail, and nothing behind it asked whether the version was still wanted.** Measured in CI run 34772700962 (`StreamCrashDurabilityTest`): the blueprint rolled back, `handleAppBlueprintRemoval` removed the `SliceTargetKey`, the UNLOAD commands timed out (`Consensus apply timed out after 30000ms`), and 123ms later a node logged "KV claims ACTIVE … not loaded locally — redeploying" and served the slice. Three producers, all fixed here: the node's KV-convergence redeploy, pending-LOAD replay and live ACTIVATE started a slice on the strength of a `NodeArtifactKey` alone; the orphan sweep walked the leader's in-memory `sliceStates` and dropped the entry BEFORE issuing the UNLOAD, so one timeout meant the key was never looked at again; and the unload chain's endpoint "unpublish" wrote `NodeArtifactValue(ACTIVE, methods=[])` between the UNLOADING put and the key removal — a claim the redeploy path then healed into a running slice.
- One predicate, `CommittedSliceTarget.permits`, read from the committed KV store and never from a projection: a version is permitted while the committed `SliceTargetKey` names it, or while a rolling update's `VersionRoutingKey` names it as the old or new version. An absent target permits nothing. [mechanism: `aether/aether-deployment/src/main/java/org/pragmatica/aether/deployment/CommittedSliceTarget.java`]
- The node refuses to load, activate or redeploy a version the predicate does not permit, and writes nothing on refusal. [verified: `aether/aether-deployment/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/deployment/node/fsm/NodeDeploymentStateRollbackOrphanTest.java` — `RedeployAfterRollback`, `LoadAndActivateAfterRollback`, each with a positive control showing the same drive reaches the `SliceStore` when the target is committed]
- **A refusal is deferred, not final.** The first CI run of this fix (34785390505, `SliceMediaTypeTest`) showed a follower applying the leader's LOAD 4 ms before it applied the `SliceTargetKey` put the leader had already acted on; the gate refused and nothing re-checked, so the slice never loaded. The store a node reads is the one the consensus applier writes (the same `KVStore` instance `RabiaNode` drives), but a follower's applied set can still lack an earlier put when a later command runs. So a refused start is parked in `NodeDeploymentState.Active.deferredStarts` and re-driven through the same gate when a `SliceTargetKey` or `VersionRoutingKey` for that artifact base arrives (`NodeDeploymentManager.onSliceTargetPut`/`onVersionRoutingPut`, wired in `AetherNode`); a newer put or a removal for the key drops the deferral, so the leader's UNLOAD for a rollback leftover wins over any later target. The deferral rides a quorum cycle with the suspended slices (`Dormant` carries it into the next `Active`): an ACTIVATE or an ACTIVE claim has no other route back, since the leader re-issues neither and only LOAD keys are rescanned on re-entry. `Dormant` ignores puts and removals, so on re-entry every carried deferral whose key the committed store no longer holds at the deferred state is dropped — a leftover the sweep removed meanwhile is not re-driven into a slice the leader never allocated. [verified: `NodeDeploymentStateRollbackOrphanTest.DeferredStart` — LOAD/ACTIVE-claim/old-version applied before the target or routing entry, re-driven on its arrival; a target for another base or another version does not re-drive; an UNLOAD in between is not undone by a later target; `DeferredStartAcrossQuorumCycle` — ACTIVATE and ACTIVE-claim deferrals survive `QuorumDisappeared`/`QuorumEstablished`; a deferral whose key was removed during Dormant is not re-driven] The `AetherNode` wiring of the two observations is pinned through a booted single-node cluster, applying the puts through the node's own `KVStore` and reading the FSM's own log lines. [verified: `aether/node/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/node/DeferredStartRedriveWiringBootTest.java`]
- The leader substitutes UNLOAD for ACTIVATE under the same predicate when a LOADED slice reports in. [verified: `ClusterDeploymentStateActiveTest.RollbackActivateSubstitution`]
- `StaleEntryCleaner.cleanupOrphanedSliceEntries` now walks the committed `NodeArtifactKey` entries and re-issues UNLOAD (or the removal, for a key already at UNLOAD or UNLOADING) on every reconcile tick until the key is absent from the store. UNLOADING is deliberately included: the node's own key removal spends its consensus retries under a timing-out consensus and nothing else re-issues (measured in CI run 34788864919, a key stuck at UNLOADING for the whole 4-minute wait). Keys of departed nodes stay with `cleanupStaleNodeArtifactEntries`. [verified: `ClusterDeploymentStateActiveTest.RollbackOrphanSweep` — re-issue on a second sweep, stop once the key is gone, no-op while core membership is unresolved, re-issue after a failed consensus write, UNLOADING removed until gone]
- The core node's teardown chains no longer write an ACTIVE claim. The `unpublishEndpoints` step is removed from the unload, deactivate, force-cleanup and activation/reactivation-failure chains: `EndpointRegistry` ignores empty-method puts, the transitional put before it already carries an empty method list, and the unload's Remove is what unregisters. [verified: `NodeDeploymentStateRollbackOrphanTest.UnloadPath.unload_neverPutsActive`]
- A rolled-back rolling update now removes its `VersionRoutingKey` in the rollback batch, after restoring the old target — the same end `complete` gives a finished update. `ROLLED_BACK` is terminal, so nothing else would ever remove it, and while it existed the rolled-back new version stayed permitted to start and stayed allocated (the leader skips deallocation while `activeRoutings` holds the base). Request routing never read the entry (`activeRouting` filters terminal deployments). The order inside the batch is load-bearing: the leader's `handleRoutingRemoval` deallocates every version the committed target does not name at that moment. [verified: `aether/aether-invoke/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/update/SliceTargetOverridePreservationTest.java` `rollback_removesTheRoutingEntry_afterRestoringTheOldTarget`; `aether/aether-deployment/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/aether/deployment/CommittedSliceTargetTest.java`]
- `KVStore.installSilently` overlays the restored snapshot and then drops the keys it lacks, instead of `clear()` then `putAll()`: a concurrent reader never sees an empty store mid-install. [verified: `integrations/cluster/src/test/java/org/pragmatica/cluster/state/kvstore/KVStoreInstallOverlayTest.java` — the restored map's iterator reads the store back on every step of the install]
- **Guarantees, stated per mechanism, with their preconditions.** A node that has *applied* the rollback's `SliceTargetKey` removal never starts that version again: every start reads the committed store after that apply, and Rabia's total order places any later LOAD/ACTIVATE/ACTIVE put after the removal. The precondition is doing the work — the follower in run 34785390505 lacked an earlier put while holding a later one, and whether that anomaly can also apply a Remove late or drop it is not established here (ticket drafted in the fix report). The gate does not by itself keep a legitimate deploy from starting: a start refused before its target is applied is re-driven when the target arrives. Orphaned keys are removed *eventually*, and only while a leader holds quorum and consensus progresses — the sweep runs inside the leader's `Active` state, refuses to act until core membership is resolved, and each UNLOAD is a consensus write that can fail and be re-issued on the next tick. No time bound is claimed.
- Not changed here: the worker's own teardown (`WorkerDeploymentManager.teardownSlice`) still forwards the same ACTIVE-with-no-methods put before its removal — a separate ticket is drafted in the fix report. The typed "no target" `StreamAddressError` for a slice whose owning blueprint is gone is deferred until #1066 (PR #1071) merges; until then the bare-alias fallback in `BlueprintStreamAddresses.engineKeyFor` is unreachable from a deployed slice only because the node no longer starts one. `[design intent — unverified]`
- Fixture corrections in existing tests, each stated: `NodeDeploymentFsmTest.KvConvergenceRedeploy`, `ActivationRaceNotFatalTest` and `NodeDeploymentManagerTest` drove starts with an empty KV store, which after this change is the rollback-leftover state rather than a live deployment; they now seed the committed target they always described. `RetryExhaustionTerminalTest`'s "terminal must hold" assertion rejected any command for the artifact; after this change the reconcile issues an UNLOAD for the leftover LOAD key (a teardown, the opposite of a re-drive), so it now rejects LOAD/ACTIVATE only.

### Fixed (2026-09-13 — #1067: config-section preflight rejected deploys the runtime would accept)
- **A blueprint whose slice declares a resource's config section only in its own jar's `META-INF/resources.toml` was refused at deploy with HTTP 500 (`MissingConfigSection`), although the slice loader resolves that section.** `ConfigSectionPreflightValidator` checked only the leader's node composite (KV overlay ⊕ `node.toml`), while `SliceStore` has layered the jar's `resources.toml` beneath that composite at load since the same commit that added the check (`265748fbd`). `DurableEntityForgeTest` and `DurableEntityTimerDurabilityTest` failed in setUp on exactly this: `test-entity` ships `[entities.orders]` only in its jar. [verified: `BlueprintPublishOwnershipTest.ConfigPreflight.publish_succeeds_whenDeclaredSectionShipsOnlyInTheSliceJar` and `publishFromArtifact_succeeds_whenDeclaredSectionShipsOnlyInTheSliceJar` red at the rc4 tip, green after]
- The preflight now checks each slice over the loader's own layering, calling the loader's functions rather than a copy of them: `SliceStore.readSliceResourcesToml(URL)`, `SliceStore.sliceIntrinsicLayer` and `SliceStore.layerSliceComposite`, which `SliceStore` itself now uses at load. **Guarantee:** a deploy is refused iff some declared section is absent from every layer the loader would consult for that slice, as seen from the leader. The view is per slice, so one slice's jar never satisfies another. A jar `resources.toml` that does not parse contributes no layer, matching the runtime's fallback to the node composite. [verified: `ConfigSectionPreflightValidatorTest.SliceJarLayer`]
- **The loader itself read the intrinsic layer through the composed slice classloader, which also holds every `[slices]` dependency jar — so a slice shipping no `resources.toml` of its own silently took the first dependency jar's file as its intrinsic layer, and provisioned a section the preflight (reading the own jar alone) refused.** Fixed on the runtime side: `SliceClassLoader.sliceJarUrl()` names the slice's own jar (the first url, by construction at every production site) and `SliceStore.readSliceResourcesToml(URL)` reads `META-INF/resources.toml` from that jar alone, closing the throwaway classloader afterwards — the one function both the loader and the preflight now call. A dependency slice's file is never this slice's layer; a loader built without a jar has an empty layer. [verified: `SliceStoreTest.buildSliceCompositeFromClassLoader_ignoresDependencyJarToml_whenOwnJarShipsNone` red at `284547461`, green after; reading through the composed loader again reddens exactly it; `SliceStoreTest.buildSliceCompositeFromClassLoader_readsOwnJarToml_ignoringDependencyJar` and `SliceClassLoaderTest.sliceJarUrl_isTheFirstUrl_andDependencyUrlsAppendAfterIt` pin the own-jar-first convention]
- A slice jar located at expansion but not at the preflight's second locate is still left unchecked rather than failing the publish (the pre-#1067 behaviour); `BlueprintService.loadSliceJar` now logs that skip as such, and the comment states that `BlueprintExpander.expand` has already refused an unlocatable jar, so the branch is only reachable by an eviction between the two locates `[unverified: not inducible in the unit fixture]`.
